title: Option C sky card is a second fully coloured panel on Plan (THE RULE)
rec: Make the sky card a plain item-78 box (white, 1.5px var(--chip-line) or teal var(--wx-line) outline, radius var(--r-panel)=20px, not the bundle's 14px) and reuse item 87's .rwx-scene technique: a sky layer only behind the top, masked with mask-image:linear-gradient(#000 55%,transparent), so the card reads white like the Weather box. corr: The finding is real, but it overstates two things. (1) It is not a hidden defect. HANDOFF.md:53 (section B1) asks this exact question and already suggests the same fix ("a plain white card whose top is the sky"). Item 99's acceptance (HANDOFF.md:106) requires B1 to be resolved before shipping. The placement source of truth, real/front-c.png, also shows the card as a plain white box with a light outline; only the bundle's .fw-wx CSS paints the full fill. So the finding should be framed as answering B1: the bundle CSS as shipped breaks items 1 and 78, and item 99 must override it. (2) Severity: medium (a plan step that will not work as written) rather than high. Nothing breaks and the plan itself already makes this a gate. Keep the recommendation: a white item-78 box, 1.5px var(--wx-line) outline, radius var(--r-panel) of 20px, and the sky as a masked top layer like .rwx-scene. Log it in QUEUE_LOG as a reaffirmation of items 1 and 78.

Three parts are overstated. (1) It is not an unnoticed defect. It is not that the page goes from one tint to two. (2) This is not a hidden defect. HANDOFF.md B1 (line 53) raises exactly this question and suggests the same fix, and item 99's acceptance (line 106) requires it resolved. Also, the placement screenshot real/front-c.png shows the card as a plain white outlined box. The full sky fill comes only from the bundle CSS and the review.html overlay. Because of this, medium fits better than high: build 99 as written with the bundle's .fw-wx background, and the result is a visible spec deviation, but it is already flagged for the app chat to resolve and would not break the app. Fix: wrap the sky in a white box with var(--r-panel) and a 1.5px outline, and give the .fw-wx layer the .rwx-scene mask (or override its background to fade to var(--panel)). Log this in QUEUE_LOG as the item-1/78 decision.

title: fred appears twice on Plan after Crunch (sky card + weather card)
rec: Decide in item 99 what the sky card does after Crunch: hide it (or collapse it to a still, fred-less line) once #results shows, since the weather card then carries the forecast and fred. Add a test: after Crunch the page has exactly one FW.bird.
ev: After Crunch on origin/main the ticket, Settings and Crunch stay and #results renders below on the same page (measured on nmain/null.html, athlete A, 390x844: ticket y79, #crunchBar y478, #results/#rWeather y644; scratchpad/review/spec/main-after-crunch.png). Item 99 puts fred in a sky card between the ticket and Settings; item 98 puts fred in #rWeather. Both are on one scrolling screen, both with looping skies.
corr: The substance is right, but high overstates it. Medium fits better: the plan is underspecified and the duplication would be visible, but it does not break the app or touch data. It is also only partly a same-viewport problem. Crunch scrolls #results to the top, so the sky card usually sits above the fold, and the two show together only while the rider scrolls between them. The handoff never says whether "screen" means the page or the viewport. Recommendation as stated: in item 99, decide what the sky card does once #results is shown. Either hide it, or reduce it to a still line without fred, or use the existing wxSky(k,{fred:false}) option the style guide names for one of the two. Then add a test that the Plan page has exactly one fred (or Kitty during takeover) after Crunch.

The problem is real, but I would rate it medium, not high: a plan step that will not work as written plus a visible duplicate. It breaks nothing in the app or in user data, and the broken rule is a decision in the handoff, not a QUEUE.md rule. The recommendation is fine. Item 99 should say the sky card collapses or hides, or drops fred, while #results is shown and not stale, and that it comes back when results hide (sport change, new ride, stale plan). Add a test that the Plan view holds exactly one FW.bird before and after Crunch. Also say where the crew strip goes ("Below Crunch the plan"), because after Crunch that spot sits between #crunchBar and #results.

Mostly right, but the severity is too high. I'd call it medium, not high. It is a gap in the plan that conflicts with a rule from the handoff, and nothing would break: no data, privacy or crash risk. Two details are not quite as stated. (1) Right after Crunch the page scrolls #results to the top (scrollY 569), so the sky card, which would sit around y380–530 plus its own height, starts off screen above. Both freds show in one 844 px view only while the user scrolls between them. Under a strict "per viewport" reading it is sometimes OK. Under a "per page" reading it is a violation. The handoff doesn't say which it means, and Mark should decide. (2) The crew strip in item 99, "below Crunch the plan", would also sit between #crunchBar and #results after Crunch, so the same after-Crunch decision should cover it. Recommendation: item 99 should say what happens to the sky card once #results shows. It could hide, or fold to a still line without fred. Add a test that counts fred drawings on the Plan page before and after Crunch, and in the KOM Kitty takeover too, since Kitty replaces fred in both cards.

title: Front page loops on plain page load break item 85 motion rules
rec: Get Mark's explicit OK as a named exception, or make the front page still by default: crew and fred drawn still, at most one one-shot (e.g. fred one hop when the forecast changes), loops only in the weather card that item 87 already allows. Record it in item 99 the way items 87-93 listed the rules they change.
ev: QUEUE.md:1266-1268 (item 85: only one thing moves at a time, only when something changed; no motion on scroll or plain page load except Crunch). Items 87/88/90 relaxed this only for the weather sky, Volume and Journal first-view entrances (QUEUE.md:1365-1368). Measured in review.html Option C with motion on: 13 infinite animations running at once (wx-drift 3, ch-bob 5, ch-blink 2, ch-pump 2, ch-sway 1) on the Plan page with no change in data. Under prefers-reduced-motion: 0 (correct).
corr:
The conflict and the 13-loop count are correct, but the loops are clearly intended, not an accident. Mark approved fred world to ship to everyone. Item 104 adds a 'Motion > Animate the world' switch, which assumes idle loops. The loops pause off screen (fw-paused, review.html:252-254) and stop under Reduce Motion. So this is a real rule conflict the handoff fails to name, and Mark should approve it explicitly. Severity is high only because it overrides a rule Mark set without saying so. Nothing breaks.

Fix: list it in items 97/99 as a named item-85 exception, the way items 87-93 did ("idle loops on the front-page sky card and crew strip"). Reuse loopWhileVisible from item 86 instead of a second observer (review.html has its own IntersectionObserver). Or tone it down as the finding suggests. Two changes are not verified: whether 13 concurrent loops cost much on an older iPhone, and whether the app build would pause them correctly.

The finding is partly right and over-rated.

(1) The sky card's own loops already have a precedent. Item 87 brought back continuous sky loops on purpose (QUEUE.md about line 1373: "This brings animated skies back on purpose"; rays turn every 40 s, the glow pulses every 5 s). A front-page sky card built from the same wxSky is close to that precedent. The parts the rules really don't cover are the crew strip's idle loops (bob, blink, pump) and fred's bob on the Plan page. These also break item 85's "one thing at a time".

(2) Mark approved fred world, idle loops included. HANDOFF.md:16 says "Respect Reduce Motion everywhere". HANDOFF.md:33 lists "idle loops" as part of the shipped CSS. Item 104 makes "Animate the world" a switch that is on by default. So the issue is mainly a missing named exception, which section B5 asks the app chat to flag. It is not a rule broken against Mark's wishes. Rate it medium, not high.

Recommendation: ask Mark to confirm the exception in the B reply. Record it in item 97/99 the way the block above item 87 does, for example "item 85's no-motion-on-load and one-thing-at-a-time rules change for fred world idle loops". Then gate the loops on the item-86 observer and the settings.worldMotion switch. Making the crew still by default is a fallback, only if Mark says no.

The conflict is real, but high severity is overstated and "make the front page still" should not be the default fix. Nothing breaks: Reduce Motion gives 0 loops, and before Option C is scrolled into view only 2 loops run (ch-pump), not 13. Mark also chose Option C on a review page that says "the animated parts are live" (review.html:162), and he says the work is approved to ship to everyone. So he has seen these loops. What is missing is only the written exception. Rate it medium, as a plan step that silently breaks a written rule. The fix: in items 97 and 99, write down which item 85 rules change, the way QUEUE.md:1365-1367 does. That is idle loops on the Plan page's sky card and crew strip, paused off screen via loopWhileVisible and governed by settings.worldMotion together with motionOK(). Confirm that with Mark. Making the page still (fred hops once only when the forecast changes) is one option to offer him, not the required fix. An open question for Mark: whether the five crew figures should share one bob rhythm or stagger it (review.html staggers them, --d: -0.6 s steps), given item 85's "one thing moves at a time".

title: White 'My Journal' over the World scene fails AA
rec: Add item 91.5's dark bottom fade and title text-shadow to the World style, and add a contrast check for the title over day, dusk, night and every holiday SKY value.
ev: Item 83: 'My Journal' white 34px/800 bottom-left. Scene day sky linear-gradient(#9FD9EE,#E6F6FB) and ground var(--w-paper) #FBF6EC (fred-world.css .scene vars). White on #9FD9EE is about 1.6:1 and on #FBF6EC about 1.06:1; large text needs 3:1. Item 91.5 solved the same problem for photos with a gradient to rgba(0,0,0,.35) plus text-shadow; item 101 says nothing.
corr:
The problem holds, but the recommendation should point at what the app does now rather than item 91.5's fixed fade. origin/main already has an adaptive scrim, jhpScrim (index.html around line 14104). It measures the pixels under the title's own letters and sets a black title background (--jh-a) just dark enough for 3.1:1, and does the same for the compact bar's 17px title at 4.5:1 (--jh-ca). Item 101 should reuse that scrim on the World header, measuring a rendered frame of the scene, which can change with sky, season or holiday. That is better than adding a fixed gradient plus a text-shadow, which would still need checking against the paper ground.

The compact bar (item 90.3) also needs to be covered: its 17px title needs 4.5:1, not 3:1. Another option is to keep the crowd and the bright ground out of the title's box when cropping. Holiday skies were not checked.

Most of the finding holds, with two corrections. First, not every sky fails: night (#1B2A55 to #3D5288, line 131) is dark enough for white text, but day, dusk and the paper ground fail. Second, item 91's fix is more than a fade plus a text-shadow. The photo style also puts a measured scrim band behind the title (--jh-a, background rgba(0,0,0,var(--jh-a)) with a box-shadow, index.html:5907 and 5956). The World style should reuse that mechanism, or give the title a dark halo or a fade, and then measure the contrast for day, dusk, night, the night-mid and night-dark ground variants, and each holiday sky (for example 'gold').

- The title sits mostly over the light paper ground and the crew, not the sky. The measured median contrast is about 1.9-2.2:1 across day, dusk and night, with a minimum of about 1.1:1.

title: Sky card text is unreadable in Run mode
rec: In item 99, either hide the sky card in Run mode or give it run-theme values (sky mixed into --panel, text pinned to a dark ink on light skies). Add a run-mode case to the contrast test.
ev: Run mode puts html.run-theme on Plan (main index.html:3225: --page #26262C, --panel #34343C, --text #F2F2F7). Rendering FW.wxSky inside nfw/null.html with run-theme: '52°' becomes rgb(242,242,247) on the sky's fixed #D3DAE0 to #fff gradient, about 1.26:1 contrast; the sub-line stays #3A3A3C (scratchpad/review/spec/sky-runtheme.png). The bright card also sits on the graphite page.
corr:
The finding holds, but two details need softening.
(a) Whether it shows depends on how the card is built. It only happens if item 99 uses the bundle's own reading. If the app passes {read:false} and draws its text with its existing r-wx run-theme rules, the temperature stays readable. The bright sky on the graphite page remains either way.
(b) Severity fits medium (a visible AA failure, and a plan step that misses the run theme) better than high. It does not break the app or touch data. It does fail the handoff's own AA check.
The recommendation should point at the existing pattern in index.html:5386-5402: under html.run-theme, mix the sky into --panel at 26%, give the text the panel halo, dim the clouds, and hide the sky when color-mix is unsupported. That beats hiding the card in Run mode. Add a Run-mode case to the contrast test, and apply the same rule to the item 98 weather card on Plan results.

The problem is real, but I'd rate it medium, not high. Section F of HANDOFF.md ('AA contrast' on every item) and the QUEUE.md contrast rules (line 91; line 701 for Run mode) would catch it during the build. So it is a visible defect, and a plan step that's incomplete as written, rather than something that breaks the app. Item 98 has the same exposure: the Results weather card also takes the Run-mode theme, and the fw-wx text colours would hit it. The fix should reuse the app's existing Run-mode sky rules at index.html:5386-5402 (sky mixed 26% into --panel, the @supports fallback, the text halo) rather than invent new values. The sub-line should be pinned to a theme token instead of #3A3A3C. Add Run-mode cases to the contrast test for items 98 and 99.

The substance holds, with a few small corrections. The rendered text is the bundle's default '55° → 60°', not '52°', because wxSky ignored the temp option I passed. The sub-line's #3A3A3C is still readable on the light sky; only the temperature fails. Only the Plan/front-page sky card (item 99) is affected. The item 98 weather card on Results is not, because run-theme applies to Plan only. The fix can reuse the app's existing run-theme sky treatment from index.html:5386-5402: mix the sky into --panel and outline the text. Severity sits between medium and high: it fails the handoff's own AA acceptance criterion in every run session, but it does not break anything.

title: fred in the weather card covers the sun and the two-temperature reading
rec: Move fred down into the space the reading leaves (or into the icon-square slot), move or drop the app's sun disc when fred is present, and add QA for a two-temperature reading at 320/390 x 100/200%. Keep fred's z-index below the text feather from item 87.4.
ev: Item 87 sun disc: .rwx-sun{right:8px;top:-2px;56px} and heat sun right:-8px;top:-26px;76px (main index.html:5417-5418; fred-round 10-15 p2 shows both top right). The review placement puts fred at card x 242-328 of 358, y 7-93, right on top of the sun. With the standard reading '58° → 66°' (.rwx-temp 2.75rem) fred collides with '66°' already at 390px/100% text, and also at 320px and at 200% (text ink rects vs fred bbox: collides=true in all four; scratchpad/review/spec/wx-fred3-390-1.png, wx-fred3-320-2.png). real/res-weather.png only shows a one-number reading (55°), which hides the collision.
corr:
The text collision is real at 100% text: badly at 320 px, slightly at 390 px (about 10 px of overlap with the '6' of 66°). Three parts of the finding are overstated.

1. Not all four cases collide. At 200% text the real reading wraps onto two lines (.rwx-temps flex-wrap: 58° on one line, the arrow and 66° below). At 390 px/200% nothing collides. At 320 px/200% fred's box touches only the corner of '58°', with little or no ink overlap (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-markmccabe-code-fuel/778ef389-720f-478d-a2c4-5f058b65c054/scratchpad/review/refute98/wx-320-2-sun.png). The reviewer's four 'collides=true' results came from injected markup that is wider than the app's: both temperatures at 2.75rem and a text arrow.
2. The sun overlap is unverified. I could not render the sun sky because wxSkySet is not a global. From the CSS alone (main index.html:5417-5418: .rwx-sun right:8px top:-2px, 56 px), the sun sits at card x 294-350, y -2 to 54, so fred's box (241-327, 8-94) would cover roughly the sun's left half. Whether fred standing in front of the sun is wrong, rather than intended, is a design call. The handoff puts the key light at the upper right.
3. The fix should target the 100% case. Place fred by measuring where the reading ends (for example, hide him or move him down when the second temperature is shown and the free width is under about 90 px). QA the two-temperature reading at 320 and 390 px.

With the app's real markup (second temperature at 2.375rem, SVG arrow), the standard '58° → 66°' at 390 px and 100% only touches fred: the boxes overlap by 7 px and the glyphs do not overlap. 'collides=true in all four' is wrong for 390 px at 200%, where the reading wraps and nothing collides. Real collisions:
- 320 px, 100%, any two-temperature reading: fred covers the second number.
- 390 px, 100%, a three-digit start (101° → 94°).
- 320 px, 200%: fred's box overlaps the first number even when the reading has one temperature.
The sun-disc overlap is real geometry on sun and heat skies only; whether it looks wrong is unverified. The recommendation still stands: fred needs a rule that keeps him clear of the reading (measure how wide the reading is, or move him down or out of the way at narrow widths and large text), plus QA of two-temperature readings at 320 and 390 px, at 100% and 200% text.

Mostly right, with two caveats. First, I could not reproduce the 320 px and 200%-text results myself; I'm relying on the reviewer's probe and on the fact that a wider reading only makes the overlap worse. Second, the sun overlap I took from the CSS anchors; I did not render a sunny sky with fred to see it. The fix should also cover the run's graphite card and the takeover period, when Kitty is drawn in fred's place in the weather card.

title: Item 98 adds a night sky that item 87 ruled out
rec: Flag both as changes to item 87 for Mark to approve, and list them in item 98 the way item 87 listed the v3-3 changes. If approved: night still under Reduce Motion, fog stays over the tiles but under fred.
ev: QUEUE.md item 87.1(i) and fred-round 10-15 p3 row 9: a clear night gives no sky and keeps the static moon icon; item 87 QA: 'A night ride shows no sky.' main index.html:10646 WX_SKIES has no night, and wxSkyPick returns null at night. Item 98 says 'a clear night → night', 'night stars twinkle', and 'add night' to ?sky=. The fog line also reverses item 87.2 (fog drifts over the whole box, tiles included).
corr: Keep the night half at medium. Item 98 adds a 'night' sky with twinkling stars and a ?sky=night option, and item 87.1(i), its QA line and fred-round 10-15 p3 row 9 rule that out. It should be flagged for Mark's approval as a change to item 87, and it must also give a still frame under Reduce Motion. Drop the fog half or soften it to low: 'fog behind fred' does not reverse item 87.2. Item 98 should just say that fog still covers the tiles (as in item 87.2) and sits under fred.

Keep the night point but present it as an intended change that is not written down, not as something 87 "ruled out" that the design chat broke by accident. The handoff's decisions table (line 25) and WX_KINDS show night was chosen on purpose and approved. Item 98 should say it supersedes 87.1(i) ("no sky; keep the moon") and the 87 QA line "A night ride shows no sky". It should also say wxSkyPick must return 'night' instead of null, and that WX_SKIES / WX_SKY_Q need 'night' added. Under Reduce Motion, night should show a still frame with no twinkle. Drop the fog claim. "Fog behind fred" fits with 87.2's fog over the whole box, tiles included, so the only note needed is to keep 87.2's coverage and put fred above the fog layer. Severity low to medium (spec bookkeeping and a QA line that changes), not a rule broken without approval.

Mark should approve it as a change to item 87, and the night stars should stay still under Reduce Motion. The fog part is wrong as stated. "Fog behind fred" puts fog in order with the new fred figure and does not take it off the tiles, so it does not reverse item 87.2. At most it is a note: keep 87.2's coverage over the whole box, tiles included, with fred above the fog.

corr: One detail is wrong. Main has no "Upcoming re-checks" of the weather to fit with. The re-check at line 14515 runs every minute and only moves entries from Upcoming to Check in. It never fetches a forecast. The recommendation stands: item 99 should say when to fetch (on Plan open, throttled, sharing fetchWeather's key and the hour-old rule, wxOld/q63), what the card shows with no forecast, offline or with no place, and that it reuses wxSkyOf/wxSkyPick. Item 101 should fall back to the plain day scene when no forecast is cached. I did not run the app; this is from reading the code.

One addition to the recommendation: the app already keeps a forecast cache in localStorage. WX_CACHE_KEY holds up to about 12 entries, written by wxCachePut and read by wxCacheGet/wxCacheFind at lines 13117-13122. Each entry is keyed by place|date|start|duration and holds wxLast (without pts) and a timestamp. Item 99 could first read the cached entry for the Plan's current inputs, so there is no network call on Plan open. It would then fetch only through the existing throttled path (wxOld and the 1-hour re-check from q63), and show the no-forecast state when neither is available. Line 12922 also documents the existing offline fallback, which uses the last forecast's feels-like from #tempF; the no-forecast state should agree with it.

The core claim holds; one detail needs fixing. No Upcoming forecast re-check exists to fit with: line 14515 is the journal-state tick. The real points to reuse are the q63 one-hour staleness rule (wxOld, line 13183) and the persisted forecast cache bluebird.wxcache.v1 (wxCacheGet/wxCacheFind, lines 13116–13124). That cache already stores wxLast without pts, keyed by place, date, start and duration. Item 99 can read it on the front page with no network call, then refresh in the background, throttled by wxOld. When there is no place, date or duration, or no cached entry, it needs a no-forecast state (no sky or number). Item 101's "today's forecast" is a new kind of fetch (today, no ride window, location source undefined), so it should default to the 'day'/season scene unless a cached ride forecast for today exists.

title: Holiday table: overlapping windows, no precedence, dates the plan can't compute
rec: Add a precedence order (warnings > own race day > birthday > care days > others; Kitty takeover vs holidays decided), one Halloween look, US-only for Thanksgiving unless locale is added, and say the sky in the weather card always stays the forecast (holiday skies only in the Journal scene).
ev: FW.HOLIDAYS (25 looks): Memorial Day (care, flag pin) and Indy 500 share the same weekend; three Halloween looks on Oct 31; Winter holidays Dec 20-26 overlaps Hanukkah and comes close to New Year's; Tour de France (3 weeks in July) covers Jul 4; Thanksgiving 'Canada: Oct' needs a locale; Kona, Tour mountain stages, Bike to Work Day, 'Your race day', 'PB / milestone' fall outside item 103's list (fixed, nth weekday, Easter, LNY, Diwali, Hanukkah, Eid). Holiday sky values (pink, green, spooky, gold, lilac) would replace the forecast sky that item 87 says comes from the forecast. No rule for holidays during the KOM takeover (Jan 5 - Mar 6 covers Valentine's and Lunar New Year).
corr:
Two parts are overstated.
1) "Your race day", "Your birthday" and "PB / milestone" don't need to be in the date table. The handoff says they come from data: the Races tab, the new profile.birthday field and the Journal. Only Kona, the Tour, the Tour mountain stages and Bike to Work Day lack a rule that can be computed. For the Tour and Kona the plan should either give the exact dates per year or drop those looks. For Bike to Work Day, "3rd Fri in May" (the US date) would make it an nth weekday.
2) The plan does not say a holiday sky replaces the forecast sky. Item 98 maps the weather card from wxSkyOf, item 99 bases the sky card on the ride's forecast, and item 101 says "sky from today's forecast". The HOLIDAYS sky field goes with the DECO backdrops. The risk is only that "show each look" is ambiguous, so the fix should be a one-line clarification: a holiday changes only fred's wear, never the forecast sky. It is not a conflict with item 87.
The precedence recommendation stands: say what wins on overlapping days, how Kitty's takeover interacts with Valentine's and Lunar New Year, and which single Halloween look shows (or whether it rotates). Thanksgiving should be US-only unless a locale is added.

Four points need correcting.
1. "Comes close to New Year's" is not a conflict: Dec 20-26 and Dec 31 – Jan 1 do not overlap.
2. 'Your race day', 'PB / milestone' and the birthday look come from user data (Races tab, Journal, profile.birthday), not from a date table. Item 103 covers the birthday separately, so their missing date rule is expected. title: KOM Kitty's 'Zwift-style' orange Z is a trademark risk; the dynamic icon can't work in a PWA
rec: Have Mark confirm the Z is acceptable, or use a different tail mark. In item 103, drop the orange-icon step now instead of 'try, then say so'.
ev: Handoff A and brand p21: an orange Z drawn in Zwift's style (not the logo file). Manifest on main has static icons only (icon-192.png, icon-512.png, apple-touch-icon index.html:14); a PWA cannot swap its home-screen icon by date. Unverified: whether a style-alike Z raises a trade-dress issue.
corr:
Keep the legal point: ask Mark to confirm the Zwift-style orange Z, or swap it for a neutral tail mark, before item 103 builds Kitty. This is unverified legally.

Restate the icon point. "Can't work in a PWA" is too strong. What is true is that an icon swap cannot be triggered by date from the client.
- On iOS, the apple-touch-icon is captured when the user adds the app to the home screen, so it will not change for people who already installed it.
- On Chrome for Android, the icon could change only by deploying new icon files or a new manifest on Jan 5 and Mar 7. Chrome then picks it up on its own manifest refresh and may ask the user to confirm.

That means two deploys a year with uneven results on each platform. Item 103 already allows skipping the icon. The improvement is low severity: decide to skip the orange icon now, or name it as a manual seasonal deploy, instead of leaving it as "try, then say so". Severity: medium for the legal question, low for the icon.

Partly overstated. (1) "Can't work in a PWA" is true on iOS. On Android, Chrome's WebAPK does eventually pick up a changed manifest icon, but on its own update schedule, often days late and possibly behind a user prompt. It cannot be timed to Jan 5 and Mar 7, and the revert needs a second redeploy. So the date-based icon is not workable as written. Doing it would mean deploying new icon files twice a year, which also changes the icon for every user and goes through item 97's icon checks. (2) The plan already treats the icon as optional. Brand p21 says "Optional orange app icon", and item 103 already says to skip it and say so. Dropping it up front is a cheap tidy-up of the plan, not a medium-severity defect. Low is fair for the icon part. (3) The Zwift-style Z is intended by design (HANDOFF A, brand p21, style-guide.md:305). The real ask is for Mark to confirm he accepts it, or to swap in a generic tail mark such as a plain bolt or a mountain. Rate it as an unverified legal question for Mark, not as a confirmed problem.

Two small corrections. First, "can't work" is slightly too absolute. A scheduled CI job could swap the icon files on Jan 5 and Mar 7. Android Chrome updates installed web app icons when the manifest's icons change, but only after a delay and usually with a prompt the user must accept (from general platform knowledge; not tested here). It would also need a sw.js cache-version bump, because the icons are precached. iOS would never update. So it is unreliable and would only reach some users, not strictly impossible, and dropping it now is still the right call. Second, severity: if Mark rules on the Z, medium is fine. Under the task's own scale, an unresolved legal question could arguably be rated high until he does.

title: Reuse loopWhileVisible instead of fw-paused
rec: Register each FW host with loopWhileVisible(el); no second observer and no fw-paused. Gate 'anim' on motionOK() && settings.worldMotion.
ev: Item 86: inView/loopWhileVisible are 'the only one in the app'. The app's .mo-off already pauses every descendant animation with !important in a cascade layer (main index.html:6098-6099, 8815). Handoff C asks for fw-paused toggling.
corr: The handoff does not ask only for fw-paused. Section C (HANDOFF.md:66) already says "Put `anim` on `<body>` when `motionOK()`; pause with the item-86 pattern", and B5 (line 57) says "Reuse the app's machinery". Only the item 97 line (HANDOFF.md:94: "`fw-paused` off screen and in background") conflicts with that. The fix is to reword item 97: register each FW host (the sky/weather host, crew, rider) with `loopWhileVisible(el)`, and do not toggle fw-paused. Put `anim` on body only when `motionOK() && settings.worldMotion`. The `.fw-paused` rules can stay in the CSS unused, because the bundle is shipped as-is and rebuilt with build-bundle.py.

This partly corrects the handoff rather than contradicting it. HANDOFF.md:66 already says "pause with the item-86 pattern"; only line 94 and the CSS's fw-paused hooks suggest a separate toggle. So the change is a clarification: use loopWhileVisible(host) for every FW host that has a loop, and leave fw-paused unused (or drop it from the CSS). Do not add a second observer. One caveat: .mo-off only pauses CSS animations. If a later version of the bundle adds a JS or Web Animations loop, it would need its own pause.

The idea is correct, but section C already asks for the item-86 pattern (HANDOFF.md:66). The real problem is that item 97's text (HANDOFF.md:94) names fw-paused instead. Change item 97 to "loopWhileVisible(host) for each FW host, no fw-paused". The fw-paused CSS rules then do nothing, but they are harmless and can stay in the bundle, since the bundle must not be hand-edited. settings.worldMotion is a new setting from the handoff (HANDOFF.md:134), not an existing one, so item 97 or a later item has to add it.
notes:
REAL: I traced it in the code and could not refute it.

1. **The app already has a pause helper.** In origin/main index.html, line 6098 has `.mo-off`, and line 6099 has the same rule inside `@layer mo-off`. It sets `animation-play-state: paused !important` on the element, every descendant and their ::before/::after. `loopWhileVisible` (8818) toggles `.mo-off` through `lvSet` (8815) when the element is off screen or `document.hidden`. A MutationObserver puts the class back after a render rewrites `className`. The weather card already uses it: `wxLoop` at 10704. QUEUE.md:1326 calls it "the only one in the app (items 87–93 reuse it)".

2. **`.mo-off` covers everything the bundle animates.** Every animation in fred-world.js is CSS: it has no `requestAnimationFrame` and no `.animate(` calls (grep count 0). The one CSS loop that uses `!important` is `animation:fw-dance ... infinite!important`. The layered `!important` rule beats an unlayered `!important` shorthand, and the comment at index.html:6093-6097 says it is built to do exactly that. So `.mo-off` on a host already does what `fw-paused` does in fred-world.css (`.fw-paused *{animation-play-state:paused!important}`). A second pause class and a second observer would be redundant.

3. **The gate matches section E.** HANDOFF.md section E says `worldMotion` is AND-ed with `motionOK()`, and `motionOK()` is at index.html:8725.

title: Item 102 trigger and place are unclear against the fixed Races order and graffiti
rec: Say: AG place 1-3 or a PR; shown on 'Ready, Freddy.' after Save (item 1.7), not on the Races tab; plays after the graffiti, once; bubbles still afterwards; share reuses the existing image path.
ev: Item 1.6: Races order is fixed (Last race card → Your bests → buttons → lists); the graffiti circle and 'PR!!' play once the first time the tab opens after a new race. Item 102 says 'a place 1–3 or a PB' without saying which placing (AG, Gender or Overall), where the scene shows, or how it sits with the graffiti pop; 'one-shot then still' conflicts with champ bubbles (ch-fizz is an infinite loop). The app says PR, not PB. A 'Save as image' (#shareBtn) already exists (item 75.5).
corr: Mostly right, with three adjustments. 1) The heading "Races: race-site win" does name the Races tab, so the scene's tab is given. What is missing is its spot within the fixed Last race → Your bests → buttons → lists order, and how it sits with the graffiti pop. Showing it on "Ready, Freddy." after Save is the reviewer's suggestion; nothing in the handoff says it. 2) The finding understates a bigger gap. The bundle has no race-site scene: no finish arch, race clock or barrier exists in fred-world.js. It has only bird({champ}) at line 31/44, a medal on riders and on fred (lines 202, 332), and a holiday medal effect (line 720). So item 102 would mean drawing new art in the app, which goes against "ship only fred-world.js/css". The design chat should supply an FW.raceSite() first. 3) The existing #shareBtn makes a Results/plan image (index.html:6361), not a race card. "Reuse the existing image path" therefore means reusing the rendering code, not the button. Item 102 should also say what happens when navigator.share is unavailable, for example falling back to a download.

Two parts need correcting.

1. The bubbles are a smaller problem than stated. The bundle can already freeze them: fred-world.css:44 pauses `.ch-fizz circle` under `.fw-paused`, and lines 45-46 turn the animation off for reduced motion. So "one-shot then still" can be built by adding fw-paused after the scene plays once. The spec just needs to say so.

2. The existing share button is not the race share. #shareBtn (index.html:6361, item 75) is the Results page's "Save as image" for a ride plan. At most its PNG-drawing code could be reused for the race card; the square race image and the `navigator.share` call are new work.

Moving the scene to "Ready, Freddy." is one possible answer, not a fix the spec requires; the item's own title puts it on Races. The real fix is for item 102 to state four things:
- which placing counts (for example AG 1–3 or a PR)
- where the scene shows
- that it plays after the graffiti pop, once
- the "PR" wording

Two parts of the finding go too far. (1) "Where the scene shows" is not fully open: item 102's title starts "Races:", so the Races tab is implied. What it leaves unsaid is where on that tab (inside or next to the last-race graffiti card, which must stay first) and how the scene is timed against the graffiti pop. Moving the scene to "Ready, Freddy." after Save (item 1.7, QUEUE.md:76) is a design choice for Mark to make, not a spec fact. (2) The existing #shareBtn is the Results plan's "Save as image": it builds the image with buildShareCard(lastResult) and names the file 'fred-plan-…png'. It is not a race share. 102 can reuse its html2canvas + canShare/navigator.share + download-fallback path, but it needs its own race card builder. Suggested wording: "AG place 1–3 (or say which placing) or a PR; plays once after the graffiti pop; bubbles stopped afterwards and under Reduce Motion; share reuses the shareBtn image/share/download path with a new race card."

title: Two sky engines: FW.wxSky duplicates the app's item-87 living sky
rec: Use FW only for the characters (FW.bird) on both the sky card and the Weather card. Draw the skies with wxSkySet. If the design wants something FW's skies add (ground strip, night), port that into WX_SC rather than shipping a second renderer.
ev: The app already has wxSkySet / WX_SC / .rwx-scene / .rwx-bg (index.html:10690, 5382–5392) with the same sky colours (#FFE9AE, #FBD0BA, #D3DAE0 …) as fred-world.css lines 4–5. The app's version handles the graphite run theme (5386: color-mix 26%), a fallback when color-mix is missing (5390), fade-morphs, and pause off screen (wxLoop / loopWhileVisible). FW's version handles none of these.
corr:
Partly overstated, and the plan already asks for most of the recommendation.
(1) The finding cites the wrong place for FW's colours: they are at fred-world.css:181-182, not lines 4-5 (those are the --w-* art tokens).
(2) "Handles none of these" is too strong. FW does have a pause hook: `.fw-paused .fw-wx *{animation-play-state:paused}` at css:253. It also turns its loops off under prefers-reduced-motion (css:254) and only runs them under an `.anim` ancestor. But nothing in FW applies the pause itself: the app would have to toggle the classes using the item-86 pattern. FW really does lack the run-theme mix, the color-mix fallback and the fade-morph.
(3) HANDOFF.md B5 (line 57) already says to check against wxSkySet and the living-sky pause, and to "Reuse the app's machinery." Item 98 (line 99) already does what the recommendation asks for the Weather card: map wxSkyOf(w) to FW.WX_KINDS, place FW.bird in the app's sky, and leave the app's reading untouched.
The open risks are elsewhere:
- Item 99's front-page sky card does not say which sky engine it uses, and the API table (line 77) offers FW.wxSky for it.
- Item 98 asks for a night sky, a fog layer drawn behind fred and outlined snowflakes, none of which WX_SC has (it has no night key).
The recommendation should therefore be narrower: state in item 99 that the sky card's sky comes from wxSkySet/WX_SC, add night and FW's ground strip to WX_SC (with run-theme versions), and drop wxSky/WX_LAYERS from the shipped bundle or keep them for review.html only.

Three parts need correcting. (1) The fred-world.css cite is wrong. Lines 4-5 are the --w-* tokens; the sky colours are at fred-world.css:181-182. (2) "Handles none of these" overstates it for pausing. FW has a .fw-paused hook (fred-world.css:253) and a prefers-reduced-motion rule (:254). It has no observer of its own, though, so the app would have to drive the pause (HANDOFF C says to use the item-86 pattern). The parts it really lacks are the run theme, the color-mix fallback and the morph. (3) Item 98 as written already says to put FW.bird into the app's existing weather card and keep the app's reading and tiles. It never says to use FW.wxSky there. The duplication risk is mainly in item 99's front-page sky card, where the handoff names no renderer and the API table (HANDOFF:77) offers FW.wxSky, and in 98's "add night". The app has no night sky: wxSkyOf returns null on a clear night, which shows a static moon (index.html:10641-10642). So "night" plus its ground strip, and the dusk ground for KOM Kitty, would need porting into WX_SC, as the recommendation says. The recommendation stands: use wxSkySet and WX_SC for the sky on both cards, use FW only for the characters, and port night into WX_SC. I did not render either sky on the run theme to see how it looks; that part is unverified.

Three parts of the finding are overstated or need adding.
(1) Pause: FW's sky is not left with no pause at all. It has a hook, `.fw-paused .fw-wx *{animation-play-state:paused!important}` (css 253), and Reduce Motion stops it (css 254). Its loops only run under `.anim`. What it lacks is its own off-screen or hidden-page detection; the app must toggle fw-paused itself.
(2) Item 98 as written already does what the finding recommends: "Place fred (FW.bird({wear: FW.WX[kind].wear})) in the sky area ... Keep the app's own reading and gauge tiles untouched." It does not tell anyone to call FW.wxSky. The real duplication risk is item 99. Its front-page sky card names no renderer, and FW.wxSky is the obvious candidate. A smaller risk is FW.wxSky shipping as dead code.
(3) The app has no night sky. wxSkyPick returns null for a clear dark window and the static moon stays. So item 98's "clear night → night" and its "fog behind fred / outlined snowflakes / night stars twinkle" need porting into WX_SC and the app CSS: a night layer, plus a fred layer between the fog and the tiles. Adding the 'night' value to WX_SKIES / WX_SKY_Q is not enough.
Recommendation: draw both the weather-card sky and the item-99 sky card with wxSkySet / WX_SC, and use only FW.bird / FW.WX[kind].wear from the bundle. Port the night sky (and the ground strip if wanted) into WX_SC with run-theme rules. Either drop wxSky / WX_LAYERS from the shipped bundle or label them preview-only. Severity: medium, as an improvement.
notes:

REAL: This mostly holds, checked against origin/main index.html and the handoff bundle. The app already has a living-sky renderer: WX_SC at index.html:10675, wxSkySet at 10690 (480 ms cross-fade morph, and it skips the fade when motionOK() is false), and wxLoop at 10704, which uses item 86's loopWhileVisible. title: The crew strip lands under the tab bar on a real phone
rec: Place the crew after .fredfoot with no background. It then shows on scroll and is fully clear of the tab bar at the scroll end (body padding already covers it: docH 975 vs crew bottom 879). Or render it only when tabbar.top − footer.bottom ≥ its height. Either way, change '…sized so nothing overlaps the tab bar' to something testable: '≥ 8 px clear of .tabbar at scroll end; hidden rather than overlapped'.
ev: Injected after #crunchBar at 390x844: crew at 719–827, tab bar at 788–844 (fixed), so the bottom half of the crew is under the tab bar at rest (shots/c-asis-390.png). At 320x568 the crew is at 728–836, entirely off screen (tab bar 512–568). It only looked clear in front-c.png because the footer was removed and that capture's ticket is 25 px shorter than the live one (ticket 79–343 in the PNG vs 79–368 live).
corr:
The problem only occurs with the page at rest; once you scroll, it goes away. The crew is ordinary in-flow content, so it scrolls clear of the tab bar. At the scroll end it sits fully above it:

- **390x844** (scrollY 151): crew 568–676, tab bar 788.
- **320x568:** crew 291–399, tab bar 512 (shots/end-320.png).

"Entirely off screen" at 320 just means below the fold. That is not an overlap.

#crunchBar is sticky above the tab bar on short screens: at 320 it measured 440–512 and at 375x667 539–611. So while scrolling, the crew also slides behind the pinned Crunch bar, not only behind the tab bar.

One part of the recommendation's reasoning is wrong. The end clearance does not come from body padding: computed body padding-bottom is 0px. It comes from .fredfoot and the page's own bottom spacing (docH 995, footer 849–893 at 390). The fixes it proposes are still sound:

- place the crew after .fredfoot, or render it only when it fits;
- give it a testable acceptance line: at least 8 px clear of .tabbar at the scroll end, hidden rather than overlapped.

At 390x844 only, the crew could also fit above the tab bar at rest if it is at most about 70 px tall.

The core claim holds, but my numbers differ. With a 117 px sky card the crew sits at 696–804 at 390x844, so 16 px of it is under the tab bar. The reviewer's 719–827 and 39 px depend on how tall the sky card ends up. At 320x568 my crew sat at 705–813, not 728–836; it is still entirely off screen. I did not check the reviewer's 'docH 975 vs crew bottom 879' figure for placing the crew after .fredfoot, so that recommendation is unverified. Also note that #crunchBar is sticky (bottom of the viewport, above the tab bar). A crew strip placed right after it can also be covered by the stuck Crunch bar while scrolling, which is another reason to put the crew after the footer or hide it when it does not fit.

What holds is that the fit is tight and the wording is vague. On a 390x844 phone, after #crunchBar and with the sky card, the crew clears the tab bar by only about 4 px at a 17%-width strip of about 90 px. A box of about 108 px, as in review.html, would overlap by about 11 px at rest. On small phones it is below the fold at rest, though fully visible and clear at scroll end. Keep the placement after #crunchBar. Make item 99's line testable, for example: "crew strip ≤ 92 px tall at 390 px, with no margin above; at rest it ends at or above .tabs top on 390x844; on any width it is clear of .tabs at scroll end; it is never covered by the sticky #crunchBar at scroll end." Severity is low, not medium.

title: No rule for the sky card when there is no forecast
rec: Add to item 99: no forecast (offline, more than 16 days out, no place) → the card stays hidden (no empty sky, no fred). Clear night → follow whatever item 98 decides for night, so the two cards agree.
ev: The live page has no network, so no forecast; after Crunch the app shows 'Couldn't get the forecast… using 75°F feels-like' (shots/crunched-1440.png). Item 87 rule 1i has no sky for a clear night, and the app uses the 75°F fallback (index.html:6195 tempF) when there is no forecast. Item 99 and the brand guide only describe the case with a forecast.
corr:
The night half of the finding is partly covered already. Item 98 (HANDOFF.md:99) says "a clear night → `night`", and FW.WX_KINDS includes night, so the weather card is decided. What is missing is only that item 99 does not say it uses the same wxSkyOf → WX_KINDS mapping as item 98. The fix is one line: "same mapping as item 98, night included." No new decision about night is needed.

The real gap is the no-forecast case. That covers offline, no place, a date beyond the forecast range, and the front page before the first Crunch. Item 99 should define the card for this case, either hidden or a neutral state. It must not show an empty sky, and it must not show a sky built from the 75°F fallback as if it were a forecast. Medium severity holds, as a plan step that is underspecified.

Some details need fixing. (1) index.html:6195 is not the fallback. The fallback is index.html:13222-13226: it uses whatever is in the #tempF field, which is 75°F only by default, and a cached forecast (wxCacheFind, 13222-13223) is used first when one exists. So "no forecast" means a failed fetch with no cache, or no Crunch yet, not simply being offline. (2) For clear night, item 98 already decides `night`, so item 99 only needs to say "use the same mapping as 98". (3) Before saying "hidden, no fred", note that the brand guide disagrees with itself. Page 26 and style-guide.md:242 list "Loading and offline: fred, idle loop", but the same table says "Empty states: no characters (decided)". Item 99 should pick one: either hide the card when there is no forecast (no cache, no place, beyond the forecast range), or show fred idle with a short line. It should also say what happens before the first Crunch. Medium severity as a plan gap is fair.

Two parts of the finding are off. (1) The clear-night case is not open. Item 98 already decides it: "a clear night → night" (HANDOFF.md:99). That replaces today's null with the static moon. So item 99 only needs to say it uses the same wxSkyOf→WX_KINDS mapping as item 98. (2) Hiding the card is only one option, and the app already has a precedent. wxCardNone (index.html:10789-10791) keeps the card and shows the fallback feels-like with "no forecast". The >16-day hint (index.html:13134) explains what fred plans for. A better rule is one shared no-forecast state for items 98 and 99, and item 98 needs it too, because it never says whether fred or a sky goes on wxCardNone. Pick one of these and apply it to both cards: hide the sky card, or show a neutral sky with no weather effects and the existing fallback line. Cover offline, more than 16 days out, and no place. Severity: medium-to-low; it is a gap in the spec, not a break.
notes:
REAL: I could not refute it. The spec gap is real. Item 99 in HANDOFF.md (line 104) describes the sky card only as "a sky card for the ride's forecast window with fred dressed for it and the reading". Neither item 99, line 18 nor section F says what the card does when there is no forecast. style-guide.md and scene-breakdown.md have no such rule either. The brand guide pages that mention the card or the sky (p03, p15–p18) also cover only the case with a forecast. p18 reads: "Sky card: Between the ticket and Settings: the ride's forecast window with fred dressed for it. fred appears only here."

The app does reach the no-forecast state. index.html:13226 shows "Couldn't get the forecast … using {tempF} feels-like instead", and index.html:6184 says tempF value=75 is "the no-forecast fallback feels-like". The Results weather card already has its own offline note at index.html:10791 ("Couldn't get the forecast. Crunch again when you're online."). title: Desktop middle column already collapses to about 95 px at 1100 px (pre-existing, not fred world)
rec: Not part of fred world, but Option C adds content to that right column. Give the middle column a floor (e.g. minmax(320px,1fr)) or raise the dk threshold, as a separate small item.
ev: origin/main at 1100x900 (html.dk): the 'No plan on screen' card wraps letter by letter ('crunc h', 'sched uled') between Upcoming and the 360 px plan column (shots/m1100-plan-view.png). Same with the bundle (shots/c-asis-1100.png). The grid is index.html:5053/5084: minmax(240px,300px) minmax(0,1fr) minmax(300px,360px).
corr: The measurement holds: 96 px, not "about 95", and the cause is as stated. One of the two suggested fixes does not work as written. Giving the middle column a fixed floor such as minmax(320px,1fr) needs at least 240+320+300 px of columns plus 48 px of gaps, about 908 px. The grid is only 804 px wide at 1100 px, so the page would overflow sideways. Two fixes would work. One is to let the side columns give up width before the middle does, for example by using fr-based maximums so they don't grow to 300 and 360 px first. The other is to raise the dk threshold to about 1300 px, where the middle column gets about 300 px. Either is a separate small item.

Mostly right, with two refinements. The collapse comes from the left track sitting at its 300px max while the middle track's floor is 0; it is not specific to the empty card, so any middle content gets the same width at 1100px. A 320px floor on the middle column would need 300+320+360+48 = 1028px of content width, or 1324px of window at full side tracks. So between 1100 and about 1324px that floor alone would make the page scroll sideways, unless the side tracks are allowed to shrink toward their 240/300px minimums. A safer fix is to drop both side tracks to their minimums below about 1280px, or to give the middle column a floor around 280px with the side tracks set to minmax(240px,300px) and minmax(300px,360px). Either fix should then be checked for no sideways scroll at 1100px, which QUEUE.md item 9 requires.

rec: Item 101 crops the scene to the crew. ev: FW.scene(): 126 KB, 1,681 nodes, 715 paths, 35 masks, 45 clipPaths, 82 running animations (190 transform and 59 opacity keyframe tracks). Main-thread cost at 1x / 4x / 6x CPU throttle: 89 / 391 / 626 ms per second, which is 1.5 / 6.5 / 10.4 ms per frame. Style and layout run on every frame (6x: 110 ms/s style, 85 ms/s layout) because CSS transforms on SVG child elements are not composited. Real WebKit on this Mac, unthrottled, 3 runs of 5 s: 54.6 / 57.6 / 59.3 fps against 60.1-60.2 fps baseline, and 60.1 fps with .mo-off (wk.mjs output). GPU raster is not included in these numbers.

The "older iPhone" claim is an inference from CPU throttling and has not been checked on a device. The core claim stands: 82 loops make style and layout run on every frame. Stopping the loops (.mo-off) removes that cost completely, so cutting or stilling the off-crop parts in item 101 is the right fix.

2. **The older-iPhone claim is unverified.** It is extrapolated from CPU throttling, not measured on a device.

2. Chromium does not drop frames, even at 6x throttle. The reviewer's own data (perf/result-chromium.json) shows the scene at 60 fps, p95 16.7 ms and 0 frames over 33 ms at 1x, 4x and 6x. - The counts are accurate: FW.scene() is about 126-129 KB, with 1,681 nodes, 715 paths, 35 masks, 45 clipPaths and 82 running animations.

- Run the header's loops only through loopWhileVisible / fw-paused.

rec: Build the scene only when the Journal header option is World, and only after first paint, through inView(el, play) or requestIdleCallback. corr:
Two parts of the recommendation need fixing.

1. requestIdleCallback is undefined in Playwright WebKit (Safari 26 user agent), so on iOS it needs a fallback. Use the app's existing inView() at /Users/markmccabe/code/fuel/index.html:8767 (FW has no inView of its own) or a setTimeout or rAF after first paint.

2. "Only when the header option is World" adds nothing: item 101 already makes the scene an opt-in Journal header option. HANDOFF B2 also already says to render "at most once per screen, only when on screen". The new and useful part is to replace "cache the string" with "keep and reuse the mounted DOM node". Building after first paint only moves the 50 ms long task to a later moment; it does not remove it.

I measured only the Chromium times (1x, 4x, 6x) and WebKit at 1x. I did not measure on a real older iPhone.

title: Caching an FW string and inserting it twice duplicates its mask and clip ids, and the visible copy then renders wrong
rec: The handoff's "cache the string" advice (B2) must be per mount. Cache by slot (header avatar, #sbAv, Closet strip), or re-key the id prefix when a cached string is reused, e.g. `s.replaceAll(oldId, newId)`. Never reuse one string in two places on the same page.
ev: Every bird, person, kitty and bike draws a fresh random id (fred-world.js:43, 97, 433, 463: `'b'+Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,7)`), so FW.bird()===FW.bird() is false. Inserting one cached riderAvatar string twice gave 6 duplicate ids out of 12. With the first copy inside display:none (as #sbAv can be) and the second visible, 1,202 px (Chromium) and 1,507 px (WebKit) of the 96 px avatar differ from a single copy: the shading masks are lost. Screenshots: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-markmccabe-code-fuel/778ef389-720f-478d-a2c4-5f058b65c054/scratchpad/review/perf/dup-zoom-chromium.png, dup-single-*.png and dup-hiddenfirst-*.png.
corr: Mostly right; three corrections. (1) WebKit did not reproduce for me: 0 px differed when I put the hidden copy first. The WebKit figure of 1,507 px is unverified. (2) In Chromium the damage is worse than "shading masks lost": the avatar's round clip and background disc are gone too, so the avatar no longer draws as a circle. (3) B2's "cache the string" advice is written for FW.scene() and the crew strip, not the avatar. The bug only appears if one cached string is inserted twice on the same page; calling FW.riderAvatar once per slot is safe. The fix stands: cache per mount, or swap in a new id prefix when a string is reused.

Partly overstated. B2 (HANDOFF.md:54) says "Render each at most once per screen ... cache the string". It never says to put one string in two places, and every fresh FW call already gives unique ids. So the fault appears only if the app reuses one cached string in two live mounts, or keeps a cached copy in a hidden view while a visible view shows the same string. The fix stays as proposed: cache per slot, or re-key the id prefix when a cached string is reused. I did not re-check the reviewer's exact pixel counts (1,202 / 1,507) or WebKit myself. I confirmed the effect in Chromium by looking at the images.

I could not reproduce the WebKit half. In my run, WebKit showed 0 changed pixels for the same test, against 1,507 in the finding. iPhone/Safari is unverified and may not be affected; the confirmed failure is desktop Chromium (html.dk layout), where the hidden header copy comes before the visible #sbAv. title: The header rider avatar loops forever on every screen

On desktop the always-visible copy is #sbAv in the fixed sidebar. On a phone it is the header .hacct circle; I did not check whether it stays on screen while scrolling. The recommendation stands: add rm to the avatar root, or render it once as a still image, and keep motion only in the Your rider sheet.

The loop is real, but the cost evidence overstates it. The 19/58/94 ms per second figures are for a full bird, not this avatar. rec: Group falling flakes and drops into 2-3 layers that each animate as one transform. That cuts the style work per frame roughly in proportion to the animation count. Budget: 15 or fewer running animations per sky card.

At 6x: snow 177 ms/s (67 ms/s of it style), wind 210 ms/s, rain 163 ms/s, fog 107 ms/s, against a 17 ms/s baseline. wx_wind is the largest at 21.8 KB, 286 nodes and 5 masks.

Wind is not 'each streak its own animation'. Only 7 of its 24 animations are streaks (5) and leaves (2). The other 17 come from the WX_CAST paceline (weather.js:40-41), the three-bike group: 9 fw-spin wheel spins, 3 fw-rock, 3 ch-bob, 1 ch-blink and 1 wx-flap. All of these run on child <g> elements inside SVG (probe3.mjs breakdown). Wind's cost also has the highest layout share (40 ms/s at 6x) because it has 285 nodes and 5 masks.

So for wind, the change that helps is cutting the cast: one bike instead of three, or static wheels on the two friends' bikes. Grouping the streaks would save at most 5 animations. title: "anim on body when motionOK()" will not work as written: motionOK() is false at load
rec: In item 97, toggle body.anim in one function called at boot, on the first tap (the MOV.live listener), on matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') change, and when settings.worldMotion changes. Or scope .anim to each FW mount rather than <body>, so loopWhileVisible and .anim act on the same element.
ev: index.html:8725 `function motionOK(){ return MOV.live && !reducedMotion(); }`. MOV.live becomes true only on the first trusted pointerdown or keydown (index.html:8834). A one-time check at boot therefore never adds .anim, and Reduce Motion is meant to be read every time. Measured: with .anim off the body, 0 FW animations run, so the bundle gate itself works.
corr: The main point is right: motionOK() is false at load (index.html:8723/8725/8834), so .anim has to be re-applied when the first tap comes and whenever settings.worldMotion changes. Two corrections to the recommendation. (1) There is no need to listen for the Reduce Motion change. fred-world.css already puts its loops under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), 11 times, so the CSS stops them however .anim is set. (2) Gating on motionOK() may be the wrong rule. The app's own looping living sky (index.html:5370-5376) does not wait for the first tap: it loops under CSS, with Reduce Motion and loopWhileVisible (8818) as the only stops. MOV.live (item 85) gates scripted moves, not ambient loops. With motionOK() as the gate, fred would stand still on every app open until the rider taps, while the sky behind him already moves. A simpler rule for item 97 that matches the app: add .anim when settings.worldMotion is on (Reduce Motion is left to the CSS). Pause each FW mount with loopWhileVisible(mount), which adds .mo-off, instead of a separate fw-paused class. Mark should decide whether fred waits for the first tap. Not run in a browser: whether the sky actually animates before a tap on a real load is inferred from the code and the comment, not measured.

The finding is right, and there is a further point. motionOK() is the gate for scripted moves that start from a tap, not for loops. In the app today, looping animations do not wait for a tap. wxLoop (10704) registers the living sky with loopWhileVisible, gated only by being on screen, the page being visible and the CSS Reduce Motion rules, so the sky moves from load. entranceOK() (8829, "these entrances play before any tap too (so not motionOK)") is the app's documented rule for motion that plays without a tap. Gating the fred world loops on motionOK() would leave fred and the crew still on the front page until the first tap, while the sky next to them is already moving. That is inconsistent with the app.

Better fix: in item 97, set body.anim from one function that uses !reducedMotion() && settings.worldMotion (no MOV.live). Call it at boot, on the matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') change event, and when settings.worldMotion changes. Pause each FW mount with loopWhileVisible (.mo-off), the same way wxLoop does, or toggle .fw-paused from it.

If Mark really wants the world still until the first tap, then the finding's recommendation applies as written: also call that function from the MOV.live listener.

The finding is right, and the problem goes further: motionOK() may be the wrong gate for ambient loops altogether. The app's existing living sky does not use motionOK(). wxLoop (index.html:10704) calls loopWhileVisible(W), and the sky's loops are stopped only by CSS prefers-reduced-motion and .mo-off. So today's sky loops run from page load, before the first tap. motionOK() is the item-85 gate for scripted moves, and entranceOK() (index.html:8829) is the separate gate for things that play before any tap. Gating fred world's ambient loops on motionOK() would leave the new sky frozen until the first tap, while the current sky in the same place already moves. For item 97 there are two options. (a) Gate .anim the same way the sky is gated today: on whenever !reducedMotion() and settings.worldMotion are true, re-read on matchMedia change and on settings change, with pausing left to loopWhileVisible on the FW mount. title: Proposed budgets for item 97 acceptance
rec: Add to section F: at most 1,200 FW nodes per screen; at most 30 running FW animations on screen at once (document.getAnimations() filtered to FW mounts); at most 4 ms main thread per frame at 6x CDP throttle with the screen's loops running; 0 FW animations running while a mount is off screen or the page is hidden; no FW insert over 50 ms at 6x (render the scene lazily). title: Item 98 maps a clear night to a twinkling 'night' sky, which reverses item 87(i), and the handoff contradicts itself

corr: The facts are right, but "high" is too strong. Mark approved fred world as a whole ("approved to ship to everyone"), and night is one of its nine skies. So this is not a break of a rule he set and still holds. It is a change to item 87(i) that the handoff never records, plus the handoff contradicting itself on whether night moves. Under the given scale that is medium: a plan step that cannot be built as written until someone decides. The recommendation stands: ask Mark whether the clear night gets a sky and whether that sky is still or twinkling. If yes, record it as a change to item 87(i) and its QA line, with a Reduce Motion still frame.

The recommendation stands: ask Mark whether the night stars twinkle or stay still, then record the answer as a change to item 87(i).

The finding is correct. Two refinements. (1) Severity is better rated medium than high. Mark approved the fred world design for shipping, and the change breaks no data, privacy or function. It is a visible conflict with item 87(i) that Mark needs to settle, and item 98 cannot be built as written until he does. (2) A detail the finding missed: in the current code, wxSkyOf(w) returns null for a clear night, not a kind. So "map wxSkyOf(w) to FW.WX_KINDS; a clear night → night" cannot work as a plain mapping. The builder would have to use wxDark(w) when the pick is null, and add 'night' to WX_SKIES for the ?sky= QA param. Whatever Mark decides, item 98 and the item 87 spec and QA lines need to be updated together, and the animated night needs a Reduce Motion frame.

title: Adding 'night' to the ?sky= param as written breaks the sky machinery
rec: Keep WX_SKIES as it is. Add a separate fred-kind function: fwKind(w) = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('sky')==='night' ? 'night' : (wxSkyOf(w) || (w && wxDark(w) ? 'night' : null)). This is the only place 'night' appears. It forces fred's night look and leaves the still moon. If Mark wants a night sky instead, add WX_SC.night, WX_IC.night and both colour rules before touching WX_SKIES.
ev: WX_SKIES (index.html:10646) has 8 values, so ?sky=night is ignored: WX_SKY_Q is null (skyq.mjs). If 'night' were added to WX_SKIES, wxSkySet(W,'night') throws 'WX_SC[k] is not a function' (verified), and wxSkyIcon('night') returns '<svg … data-k="night">undefined</svg>' (verified). There is also no .rwx-layer[data-k=night] --wx-c and no .rwx-sky[data-sky=night] --wx-ic (5387-5392).
corr: The problem is right; the main fix it recommends is weaker than it should be. Its fwKind helper keeps the still moon, which fails item 98's own requirement that "night stars twinkle" (HANDOFF.md:100). It also bypasses the app's sky code, which HANDOFF.md:57 asks to reuse. Better: first add WX_SC.night (stars), WX_IC.night and the two night colour rules (.rwx-layer[data-k=night] --wx-c and .rwx-sky[data-sky=night] --wx-ic, plus their dark-theme mix). Then add night to WX_SKIES, and have wxSkyPick return 'night' where it now returns null for a dark window. fwKind is acceptable only as a fallback that dresses fred and nothing else.

What holds: adding 'night' to WX_SKIES alone crashes wxSkySet and breaks the icon, and wxSkyOf returns null for a clear night. Item 98 needs a note saying that 'night' needs a new sky entry (WX_SC), a new icon (WX_IC) and both colour rules before it goes into WX_SKIES. It also needs a note that a clear night is detected with wxDark(w), not with wxSkyOf.

Three corrections:
(1) The handoff does not tell anyone to add 'night' only to WX_SKIES. "Add night" is underspecified, not a step that is wrong as written. This is closer to low/medium, an implementation note, than a plan defect.
(2) The main recommendation conflicts with the handoff. Item 98 says "night stars twinkle" (HANDOFF.md:100), and FW.wxSky lists night among its nine kinds (line 77). Item 98 wants a real night sky. A fred-only fwKind that "leaves the still moon" would miss the item's own acceptance. The finding's fallback should be the main path:
- add WX_SC.night (a star layer, which can reuse the bundle's twinkle CSS)
- add WX_IC.night (a moon)
- add .rwx-layer[data-k=night] --wx-c and .rwx-sky[data-sky=night] --wx-ic
- add 'night' to WX_SKIES
- have wxSkyPick return 'night' where it now returns null for a dark window. This changes the old QUEUE rule ("a clear night: null, no sky, the static moon stays", index.html:10642), so Mark should sign that change off in QUEUE_LOG.
(3) Cloudy, rainy and other non-clear nights keep their weather kind through wxSkyPick. Only the clear-night branch changes.

The problem is real, but the recommendation is only partly right. Its fwKind shortcut "leaves the still moon". Item 98 (HANDOFF.md:100) asks that "night stars twinkle", and the bundle already ships a moving night sky: FW.wxSky('night') draws a moon and stars, and 'night' is in FW.WX_KINDS (HANDOFF.md:77). So a fred-only night that keeps the app's still moon falls short of item 98.

Better wording for the item:
- Keep WX_SKIES at 8 values until night is fully in place.
- Then either add WX_SC.night, WX_IC.night, a .rwx-layer[data-k=night] --wx-c rule and a .rwx-sky[data-sky=night] --wx-ic rule (lifting the stars from the bundle) before adding 'night' to WX_SKIES, or build the night sky layer from the bundle's night sky.

title: Pausing: .mo-off already pauses FW loops, but wxLoop stops watching the box on a clear night
rec: Do not add fw-paused. Extend the wxLoop condition to include the fred layer, e.g. W.querySelector(':scope>.rwx-fred .rwx-layer'), so item 86's .mo-off covers fred.

corr: The gap is only a risk in how item 98 gets built; it does not happen for certain. HANDOFF.md:99-100 (item 98) says "a clear night → night" and "night stars twinkle". title: How to reuse the app's machinery for fred (a concrete plan)

The entrance hides only .rwx-scene and .rwx-fog (5472, 5482). Print hides only those two (5496). Both weather boxes go through wxPut: #rWeather and the run's #runWx (12859).
corr: The plan works in outline, but steps 1-2 as written have two flaws. (a) wxSkySet returns early when there is no sky ("if(!k) return", 10702), and old layers are removed when the sky is cleared. wxSkyOf gives no sky on a clear night (the static moon, comment at 10746). HANDOFF item 98 says a clear night maps to fred's 'night' kind. Built inside wxSkySet's sky path, fred would vanish on clear nights. (b) wxSkySet treats every child of .rwx-scene and .rwx-fog as old ("old=[...S.children, ...O.children]"). It keys on the sky key, not fred's kind. If the fred layer reuses mk and the fade code unchanged, every sky change re-fades fred even when his look is the same, and a fred-only change with the same sky hits the early return and is never applied. Fix: keep fred in his own container with his own data-k (FW kind plus wear), and add a separate fwSet step called from wxDress that runs even when k is ''. Do not add the fred layer to S/O's old list. Small points: HANDOFF calls FW.bird({wear}) without cast:false, so whether fred keeps his ground shadow is a design choice to confirm. Step 7 (wxCardNone and the typical card) is a real open question: wxCardNone has no data-sky today, so with this wiring it would show no fred unless fwKind is set there too.

Three details in the plan need fixing.

If the fred layer is built inside wxSkySet with the same mk code, the night case never gets fred. The fred layer needs its own key and its own early return, keyed on fwKind rather than k. Likewise, the morph short-cut at 10694 returns when the sky is unchanged; fred must not depend on it.

2. **Fog must sit behind fred.** .rwx-fog is z-index 2 over the whole box (5383), and the handoff says fog drifts behind fred. Placing .rwx-fred after .rwx-fog in the DOM is not enough on its own: it needs an explicit z-index above 2 and must stay clear of the words.

3. **One more rule needs .rwx-fred.** The run-theme @supports fallback at 5390 also hides only .rwx-scene and .rwx-fog. Add .rwx-fred there too, or decide that fred stays on graphite. This is in addition to the wx-arm, wx-go and print rules.

title: fred's ground shadow floats in mid-sky
rec: Use FW.bird({wear, cast:false}) in the weather card.
ev: In the card, FW.bird draws its .fw-cast ellipse under him with no ground beneath it (scratchpad/review/weather/card-390-1-sun.png). The API already offers cast:false.
corr: Keep the cast shadow. A smaller, valid point: outside a .fw-wx[data-k] wrapper, the per-weather shadow strength (weather.css:96-100: .17 for sun and heat, .07 for clouds, fog, rain and snow, .09 at night) does not apply, so fred keeps the default .13 (cast.css:56) in every weather. Mostly right, but there are two ways to fix it, and the recommendation offers only one. Either pass `FW.bird({wear, cast:false})` as suggested, or keep the shadow and give fred a surface to stand on (for example the `.wx-ground` strip that `FW.weather()` already draws). The `cast:false` option is the smaller change and fits res-weather.png, which has no ground. Note that the screenshot is from the reviewer's own build of item 98, not from a shipped screen. Even so, it follows item 98's wording exactly, so the shadow would float in the real build too.

title: At 200% text on 320 px the umbrella touches the card's rounded edge
rec: Inset fred so his widest look (the umbrella) clears the 20 px corner, or let the reserved column absorb it.
ev: Rain kind at 320x200%: 33 fred pixels sit at the card edge and are clipped by .r-wx overflow:hidden (probe2 'edge 33'). At 390 the umbrella reaches 355 of 358 px.
corr: Restate the finding: at the review.html placement, the umbrella look is clipped by the card's top edge and its rounded top-right corner at every width and text size (320 and 390, 100% and 200%). The umbrella's box sits about 8px above the card and 0.3px from its right edge. The cause is that the umbrella art goes outside fred's 200x200 viewBox (to y of about -14 and x of about 260 after the 10 degree rotation), not text scaling. Fix: when building item 98, inset fred at least about 10px from the top and right, or scale him down for the umbrella look. Then check the rain sky at 320 px. Severity stays low.

What does hold is a placement note, not a 200%-at-320 bug. The umbrella look (FW.bird with wear:['umbrella']) draws about 26 to 30 px past fred's own box, because his SVG has overflow:visible. In the probe, the clouds look ends at x=325 on a 358 px card, while rain reaches x=355. So the spot chosen for fred has to be sized for his widest look, not the clouds look shown in review.html:193. Otherwise the canopy comes within about 3 px of the right edge and touches the top of the card, which has overflow:hidden (index.html:5379), at any width or text size. Fix: reserve that room when placing him in item 97–104, for example by insetting fred about 30 px more or scaling the umbrella look down. Severity: low/polish. Whether the 20 px corner (--r-panel, index.html:31) actually clips the canopy is not shown: the probe never measured it, and the crops do not show it.

What holds, as low-severity polish: with the review.html placement (86 px fred, top about 2 px), the rain umbrella's top sits 1–2 px from the card's top border in every size, not only at 320/200%. Its right tip is 3 px from the right edge but below the 20 px corner. Recommendation: give fred about 6–8 px of top inset, or scale the umbrella look down, so the canopy clears the top border. The corner and the reserved column are not the problem.

area: 103 (and A: KOM Kitty, brand guide p21)
title: Seasonal KOM Kitty home-screen icon cannot work on iOS and is neither cheap nor reliable on Android: skip it
rec: Take the handoff's own way out: in 103, drop the icon swap and log in QUEUE_LOG.md that a PWA can't change its home-screen icon by date (iOS never, Android only through deploys and a user prompt). Keep the Kitty takeover in-app only (sky card, weather card). The brand guide already marks the icon as optional (p21: "Optional orange app icon"). Do not add a KOM_SEASON.icon code path.
ev: The app is static on GitHub Pages (origin/main CNAME = fuel.bluebirdmultisport.com). index.html:14 is a static <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="icon-192.png">, and manifest.webmanifest is a static file with two icons. iOS takes the apple-touch-icon once, at Add to Home Screen, and never refreshes it. Changing the link or the file later, from JS or by a deploy, does not change an installed icon. On Android, an installed app's icon comes only from the served manifest, never from a JS-swapped <link rel=manifest>, and Chrome refreshes it only on its own schedule after the user opens the app. From Chrome's documented update rules (not tested on a device), an icon change also shows the user an update prompt. A seasonal swap would therefore need two dated deploys every year (Jan 5 and Mar 7) and would reach users days late. Users who don't open the app would keep the orange icon past Mar 7. Separately, an orange tile with an orange Z on the tail resembles Zwift's orange app icon (legal judgement not verified). Renders of the Kitty tile: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-markmccabe-code-fuel/778ef389-720f-478d-a2c4-5f058b65c054/scratchpad/review/icon/kitty120.png. At 40 px the Z and the KOM KITTY lettering turn to mush: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-markmccabe-code-fuel/778ef389-720f-478d-a2c4-5f058b65c054/scratchpad/review/icon/z_kitty40.png
corr: Severity should be medium, not high. This is a plan step that won't work as written, and item 103 (HANDOFF.md:122) already says to skip the icon and say so if a PWA can't change it. Brand guide p21 calls it optional. The recommendation stands: in 103, drop the date-driven icon swap, log in QUEUE_LOG.md that a PWA can't change its home-screen icon by date, and keep the Kitty takeover in-app. One fix to the wording: the code path already exists. holidays.js:65 defines `KOM_SEASON.icon:'#F07A3A'`, so the advice should be "don't wire `KOM_SEASON.icon` to the manifest or apple-touch-icon", not "don't add it". The Android update-prompt detail and the Zwift trademark risk were not checked.

The facts are right, but the severity and framing are overstated. This is not high. It does not break the app, user data, privacy, or a rule Mark set. Item 103 as written (HANDOFF.md:122) already says to skip the icon if a PWA can't change it dynamically, so the plan does not fail as written. It reaches the "skip and say so" branch. Rate it low to medium: confirm in the review that 103 should take the skip branch now. Also remove or leave unused the `icon` field in KOM_SEASON (holidays.js:65) and the comment at holidays.js:2164, so no dead code path ships. Then log the reason in QUEUE_LOG.md. The Zwift look-alike point is a separate, unverified legal and brand question. The design chat chose "drawn in Zwift's style (not Zwift's logo)" on purpose (HANDOFF.md:24, brand guide p21). That choice also applies to the in-app Kitty, not only the icon, so dropping the icon does not settle it. Raise it with Mark as its own question rather than as part of this finding. The 40 px legibility point holds only if the icon shipped, so it does not matter once the icon is dropped.

The facts and the recommendation are right, but high severity is too much. Building 103 as written breaks nothing: the handoff tells the builder to skip the icon and say so if a dynamic icon isn't possible, and the brand guide marks it optional. So this is medium at most, a plan step that won't work as written and already has a planned exit, not a break, data or legal issue. The Zwift point is a guess. title: Generate the PNGs in a browser with fred-world.css and the app tokens loaded, from a script in the repo
rec: Add a small script, scripts/icons/make-icons.mjs, using the repo's own Playwright. It renders the inlined bundle with the app tokens and no .anim class (still), and writes icon-512.png, icon-192.png, apple-touch-icon-180.png and icon-maskable-512.png at deviceScaleFactor 1, flattened to opaque. ev: FW.bird() returns an SVG whose fills are CSS variables: var(--w-bird), --w-beak, --w-paper, --w-blush and --w-bird-wing from fred-world.css, plus var(--blue), var(--green), var(--teal) from the app (cast.js:36-75; the bundle's undefined vars are --blue, --green, --teal, --text, --font and others). A plain SVG rasteriser (sips, rsvg, ImageMagick) would draw a black or empty bird. With a Playwright page holding both CSS sources and :root{--blue:#179BCC;--green:#BECC41;--teal:#2ABCBB}, my render had no console errors and correct colours. The repo has no icon script; icon-512.png was last made by hand in commit 980bfc2.
corr: Two small refinements.
