Without a rel=icon, Chromium-based browsers request /favicon.ico, which does not exist, so they probably show a generic icon today rather than the word tile. title: apple-touch-icon points at the 192 px 'any' icon; give iOS a dedicated 180 px opaque file
rec: Add apple-touch-icon.png at 180x180 with no alpha (86% art), point the link at it with sizes="180x180", and add it to SHELL.
ev: index.html:14 is <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="icon-192.png">. iPhone home-screen icons are 180x180 (60pt@3x). icon-192.png has an alpha channel (sips: hasAlpha yes), although its corners render opaque today.
corr: The reason given is weak, but the change is still worth making for a different reason. iOS shrinks a 192 px apple-touch-icon to 180 px without trouble, so the size mismatch alone is cosmetic. The real risk comes from item 97: if the new icon-192.png is drawn with the 23% rounded corners as transparent pixels, iOS fills those transparent corners with black and then applies its own rounded mask. The home-screen icon would get black corners or a doubled, smaller rounded square. So the iOS file should be a full-bleed square on #179BCC with no alpha and no baked-in corner radius, since iOS rounds it itself. Point index.html:14 at it with sizes="180x180", add it to SHELL in sw.js, and bump CACHE. Item 97's acceptance check ('no visual change except the icon') should include viewing the icon on an iOS home screen. I did not check this on a real iPhone.

Partly overstated. The current icon-192.png is fine on iOS: it is opaque and scales down without trouble, so this is not a bug today. The real risk comes with item 97. If the new icon is drawn with 23% rounded corners that are transparent, the iOS home screen will show black corners. The iOS file should be a full square of #179BCC with no rounding (iOS applies its own mask), 180x180, with no alpha. If it is added to SHELL in sw.js, the CACHE name (fred-shell-v118) also has to be bumped or existing users will not pick it up. I did not test this on an iOS device.

The main reason for the dedicated file is that item 97's own spec (HANDOFF.md:95, "23% corner radius") would draw transparent rounded corners into the PNG, and iOS renders those as black. The 192 vs 180 size difference is minor because iOS scales the image down. Make apple-touch-icon.png full-bleed and opaque, with square corners so iOS applies its own mask. Add it to SHELL in sw.js and bump CACHE. Also add a separate maskable entry to the manifest, since it has none today.

title: Service-worker CACHE must be bumped past the unmerged q95/q96 values, and new icon files added to SHELL
rec: After 95 and 96 merge, 97 sets CACHE to 'fred-shell-v121' and adds apple-touch-icon.png, icon-maskable-512.png and the favicons to SHELL. Optionally use new file names (or ?v=2 in the manifest and link) so stale HTTP caches, such as GitHub Pages' max-age, don't serve the old PNG under the same URL.
ev: sw.js on origin/main has CACHE = 'fred-shell-v118'. Branch q95-small sets v119 and q96-sync sets v120. SHELL lists './icon-192.png', './icon-512.png' and './manifest.webmanifest'.
corr: The cache bump is right, but the list of files to add is partly invented. On origin/main, index.html line 14 is `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="icon-192.png">` and there is no `rel="icon"` or favicon link. manifest.webmanifest lists only icon-192.png and icon-512.png (purpose "any"). Item 97 only asks to regenerate icon-192 and icon-512 and to keep a maskable variant. It names no apple-touch-icon.png and no favicons. So 97 should: set CACHE to the next free number after whatever has merged (v121 if 95 and 96 both land first); add only the files it actually creates to SHELL and the manifest, most likely one maskable PNG with "purpose":"maskable"; and keep or repoint the existing apple-touch-icon link. A 180 px apple-touch-icon.png and favicons would be optional extras. Adding them is not a correction of the plan. New file names or a ?v= query are a reasonable guard against stale HTTP copies, but whether that is needed is unverified.

The new file names are guesswork, not part of the plan. On origin/main, index.html line 13 links manifest.webmanifest and line 14 sets apple-touch-icon to icon-192.png. The manifest lists only icon-192.png and icon-512.png (purpose "any"). No favicon or apple-touch-icon.png file exists in the tree. HANDOFF item 97 regenerates icon-192.png and icon-512.png in place and adds only "a maskable variant". So the only new file the plan implies is the maskable PNG. It must go into the manifest (purpose "maskable") and into SHELL. apple-touch-icon.png and favicons go into SHELL only if 97 chooses to create them. The worry about a stale HTTP cache is mostly covered already. The worker fetches same-origin files network-first with { cache: 'no-cache' } (sw.js, fetch handler), which revalidates with the server. The gap is the install step: c.addAll(SHELL) uses the default cache mode, so for a few minutes after a deploy it could store the old PNG from the browser's HTTP cache. Giving the new icon a new file name, or adding ?v= in the manifest and the link tags, closes that gap cheaply. I did not check GitHub Pages' actual max-age, or whether iOS refreshes home-screen icons for apps already installed.

Partly overstated. (1) The bump is already a standing rule: QUEUE.md:1369 says 'Bump the cache version in each item', and every done item logs it (e.g. 'Cache v118' at :1797). So the real point is only the number: v121 or later, set after 95 and 96 merge, whatever order they land in. (2) The handoff does not name apple-touch-icon.png or favicon files. Today the apple-touch-icon is icon-192.png (index.html:14) and there is no favicon. Only a new maskable PNG, plus any apple-touch or favicon file 97 chooses to add, needs a SHELL entry and a manifest entry (purpose 'maskable'). Regenerating icon-192/512 in place needs no SHELL change. The bundle is inlined into index.html, so it adds no files. (3) The cache-busting idea (new file names or ?v=) is reasonable but unverified: install uses caches.addAll (sw.js:16), which goes through the HTTP cache, and I did not measure the Pages max-age.
notes: REAL: I checked the cache values and they match the finding. `git show <ref>:sw.js` line 8 gives CACHE = 'fred-shell-v118' on origin/main, 'fred-shell-v119' on q95-small (b750e93) and 'fred-shell-v120' on q96-sync (0f64cf0). title: The 40 px in-app fred tile on sign-in/splash: does the brand rule turn it into fred, and does that break "fred at most once per screen"?
rec: Ask Mark: keep every in-app .apptile as the word tile (simplest, and what 97's acceptance implies), or switch only the 40 px sign-in tile to fred and leave fred out of the sign-in art. Log the decision.
ev: index.html:2175 sets .fred-brand .apptile to 40x40 (sign-in at 6755 and 7495). Brand guide p8 and p26 say "App tile and header (40 px and up): fred in the blue square". The header tile is 26 px (index.html:1679, 2184), so the word stays there. 97's acceptance says "no visual change except the icon". p26 also puts "Ashley and fred" on onboarding and sign-in, which would be a second fred on that screen.
corr: Two corrections. First, the 40 px tiles are not on a splash screen. They are in the Settings > Account sync card (index.html:6755) and the sync save-gate modal (index.html:7495). Second, the "second fred" conflict only applies if someone later builds the sign-in art from brand guide p26 and style-guide.md:240/295. I found no planned item that adds it: a grep of HANDOFF.md finds no sign-in or onboarding step, and Ashley shows up only in the overview at line 20. So it is a future rule clash to settle now, not something items 97-104 would break as written. Neither placement was checked in a browser.

Partly right, but only as a mismatch between documents, at low severity. Brand guide p8 and p26 and style-guide.md:236 say every app tile of 40 px and up shows fred, and p26 and style-guide.md:240 put Ashley and fred on sign-in. The app has 40 px word tiles on two sign-in surfaces (index.html:6755 and 7495). HANDOFF.md:17 and item 97's acceptance ("no visual change except the icon") already settle this: only the home-screen icon becomes fred, and every in-app `.apptile` stays the word tile. No item in 97-104 adds sign-in art, so fred cannot appear twice on those screens. Recommendation: don't ask Mark. When building 97, add one line to QUEUE_LOG.md saying that "app tile (40 px+)" in the brand guide means the home-screen icon, that in-app tiles stay the word, and that any future onboarding or sign-in art with fred must remove or replace the `.fred-brand` word tile so fred appears only once on that screen.

Two details need fixing. First, the 40 px tiles are not on a splash or a sign-in page. They sit in the Settings › Account "Back up and sync" card (index.html:6755, inside #syncCard/#syncOut) and in the sync save-gate modal (#syncGateModal, index.html:7495). Second, none of items 97–104 in HANDOFF.md section D builds the "Ashley and fred" onboarding or sign-in art, so a second fred on those screens can only happen if that art is added later. Today the only real question is whether the 40 px .fred-brand tile becomes fred. Whatever Mark decides should also cover the 26 px sidebar tile (index.html:7296) and the inline 26 px tile on the printed plan (13237), which stay as the word.

title: Under Reduce Motion the scene's entrance leaves every layer invisible
rec: In the app, never put fw-pre on a scene unless entranceOK() is true and an inView play is armed for it. On stop or Reduce Motion, take fw-pre off, following item 86's 'land at the end state' rule. Ask the design chat to make the reset win: `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:1!important}` inside the reduced-motion block and under `.rm`. Add a kit case: a Reduce Motion scene with fw-pre must show its layers.
ev: fred-world.css world.css: `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:0}` has specificity (0,3,0). The Reduce Motion reset is `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.scene .fw-L{animation:none!important;opacity:1}}` at (0,2,0), and its opacity is not !important, so the hiding rule wins. Probe review/code/probe.mjs on fwprobe/nfw/null.html with Reduce Motion on: FW.scene in `.scene.fw-wide.fw-pre`, then `.enter` added. After 900 ms all 18 .fw-L layers are at opacity 0 (probe.txt reduce.entrance.opacities=["0"]). They reach 1 only after fw-pre is taken off. The app's own `*{animation:none!important}` (index.html:4217) cannot help, because opacity is not an animation.
corr:
This is a latent integration trap, low to medium, not a high bug. The Reduce Motion reset and the `.rm` reset do not beat `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:0}` (specificity (0,3,0) vs (0,2,0), and the reset is not !important). So if the app adds fw-pre to a scene and then skips the entrance under Reduce Motion or `.rm` (for example, it arms the observer only when motion is OK), that scene stays blank. Two fixes:

1. When building 97/101, either don't add fw-pre when the entrance can't play, or always remove it the way scene.html:82 does, whatever the motion setting.
2. Ask the design chat to make the reset win, for example `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:1}` inside the reduced-motion block and under `.rm`.

HANDOFF.md should also document the fw-pre/enter contract, because it is currently undocumented. A kit case for a Reduce Motion scene that has fw-pre is a reasonable addition.

Low, defensive point only. fw-pre is an undocumented hook in the design. Its hiding rule outranks the Reduce Motion reset, so once it is on, only the app's JS can take it off. Recommendation: for item 97, document the scene.html:76-82 contract (fw-pre is removed when `.enter` is added, on first intersection). Only add fw-pre when entranceOK()/motionOK() is true; otherwise render the scene without it. A one-line CSS guard would also help: `opacity:1!important` for `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L` inside the reduced-motion block and under `.rm`. Add a kit case: under Reduce Motion, a scene in view shows all its .fw-L layers at opacity 1.

Low, polish and robustness. Scenes hide their layers with a class that only CSS knows about, `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:0}` at world.css:19. Nothing tells the app how to use it, and the Reduce Motion reset does not override it. When the app copies scene.html's IntersectionObserver pattern, it should treat `fw-pre`→`enter` as a swap, never as two classes on at once. Under Reduce Motion it should simply not add `fw-pre`, which matches item 86's land-at-the-end-state rule. Optionally, ask the design chat for `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:1}` inside the reduced-motion block, as a safety net. A kit case asserting that a Reduce Motion scene shows its layers is still worth adding.
notes:
REFUTED: The CSS part checks out. In /Users/markmccabe/Downloads/handoff/fred-world.css (source world.css:19), `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:0}` has specificity (0,3,0). The reset `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.scene *,.scene .fw-L{animation:none!important;opacity:1}}` has (0,2,0) and its opacity is not !important, so it loses. The same goes for `.rm .scene .fw-L{opacity:1}`.

The claimed failure does not happen with the design's own wiring. The probe (review/code/probe.mjs:14-15) keeps fw-pre on and adds `enter` beside it. The reference driver does it differently: /Users/markmccabe/Downloads/fred-world/fred-world/scene.html:76,82 adds fw-pre, then the IntersectionObserver removes fw-pre when it adds `enter`. Under Reduce Motion the animation is then none and nothing sets opacity:0, so the layers show as soon as the scene is in view. The finding's own probe agrees: the layers reach 1 once fw-pre is off.

The shipped JS (fred-world.js) never adds fw-pre, and HANDOFF.md never mentions fw-pre or the entrance. So a scene goes invisible only if the app adds fw-pre and then never removes it. "Leaves every layer invisible" overstates the bundle, and high severity is not supported. | correction: This is a latent integration trap, low to medium, not a high bug. The Reduce Motion reset and the `.rm` reset do not beat `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:0}` (specificity (0,3,0) vs (0,2,0), and the reset is not !important). So if the app adds fw-pre to a scene and then skips the entrance under Reduce Motion or `.rm` (for example, it arms the observer only when motion is OK), that scene stays blank. Two fixes:

1. When building 97/101, either don't add fw-pre when the entrance can't play, or always remove it the way scene.html:82 does, whatever the motion setting.
2. Ask the design chat to make the reset win, for example `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:1}` inside the reduced-motion block and under `.rm`.

HANDOFF.md should also document the fw-pre/enter contract, because it is currently undocumented. A kit case for a Reduce Motion scene that has fw-pre is a reasonable addition.

REFUTED: The CSS fact is right, but the failure only happens in a state the design's own pattern never creates. In fred-world.css, `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:0}` (0,3,0) does beat `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.scene *,.scene .fw-L{animation:none!important;opacity:1}}`, whose opacity is not !important. Nothing in fred-world.js sets or reads fw-pre, and HANDOFF.md never mentions it. The only place it is used is the reference page /Users/markmccabe/Downloads/fred-world/fred-world/scene.html:76-82. There fw-pre is added, and an IntersectionObserver removes fw-pre and adds `enter` in the same step, whatever the motion setting. fw-pre and `.enter` are never on a scene together. The probe put both on at once, which is a state the design never makes. If the app follows the reference, Reduce Motion works like this: on first view fw-pre comes off, `animation:none!important` cancels l-in, and every layer shows at opacity 1. That is the item-86 end state, so nothing is wrong. The layers can only stay hidden if the app adds fw-pre and then never takes it off, and that would happen with or without Reduce Motion. It is not a Reduce Motion bug and not a high-severity break. | correction: Low, defensive point only. fw-pre is an undocumented hook in the design. Its hiding rule outranks the Reduce Motion reset, so once it is on, only the app's JS can take it off. Recommendation: for item 97, document the scene.html:76-82 contract (fw-pre is removed when `.enter` is added, on first intersection). Only add fw-pre when entranceOK()/motionOK() is true; otherwise render the scene without it. A one-line CSS guard would also help: `opacity:1!important` for `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L` inside the reduced-motion block and under `.rm`. Add a kit case: under Reduce Motion, a scene in view shows all its .fw-L layers at opacity 1.

REFUTED: The CSS is quoted correctly. world.css:19 has `.scene.fw-pre .fw-L{opacity:0}` at specificity (0,3,0), and the Reduce Motion reset `.scene *,.scene .fw-L{animation:none!important;opacity:1}` sets opacity without !important, so the hiding rule wins on specificity.

The failure comes from how the probe was set up, though, not from how the bundle is meant to be used. The probe (review/code/probe.mjs:14-15) keeps `fw-pre` on the scene and adds `enter` next to it. The only reference use, scene.html:75-82 in the fred-world folder, swaps the classes instead: `el.classList.remove('fw-pre'); el.classList.add('enter')`. With that swap, Reduce Motion works. `fw-pre` is gone, the reset turns the animation off, and the layers show at opacity 1. The finding admits this itself ("They reach 1 only after fw-pre is taken off").

`fw-pre` is not in fred-world.js (0 matches), and HANDOFF.md never mentions `fw-pre` or the entrance. So nothing in the plan tells the app to put both classes on a scene.

It is also not a Reduce Motion bug. A scene that keeps `fw-pre` and never gets `enter` is just as invisible with motion on. With motion on, keeping both classes happens to work only because the `l-in` animation with fill `both` overrides opacity:0. "Every layer invisible under Reduce Motion" therefore happens only with a class combination that no reference code produces. High severity does not hold. | correction: Low, polish and robustness. Nothing tells the app how to use it, and the Reduce Motion reset does not override it. A kit case asserting that a Reduce Motion scene shows its layers is still worth adding.

title: The bundle script sits after the app's script, so FW does not exist during the app's first render
rec: Inline the JS block before the app's main <script> at line 8073. It has no DOM or app dependencies: no document/window access apart from setting window.FW, and no timers. Alternatively, read FW lazily and guard it with `window.FW &&`. Write the order into item 97's acceptance.

title: motionOK() is the wrong gate for loops; use !reducedMotion() and pause with .mo-off
rec: Toggle body.anim from inside the app script whenever `!reducedMotion() && settings.worldMotion` changes: on the matchMedia change listener and on a settings change. Do not tie it to the first tap. Register each loop as load-time in the motion kit's ON_LOAD_OK under item 97/98/99. Keep motionOK() for one-shots (cheer, race-site win).
ev: index.html:8725 `function motionOK(){ return MOV.live && !reducedMotion(); }`. MOV.live becomes true only on the first trusted pointerdown or keydown (index.html:8840 area). If `anim` goes on body only when motionOK() is true, fred and the crew stand still on every load until the first tap. The app's own living-sky loops run from load under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` (index.html:5457), and the motion audit allows load-time loops only through ON_LOAD_OK with their item (motion.test.mjs:28). motionOK and reducedMotion are inside the app's IIFE, not global (probe2: typeof motionOK/loopWhileVisible/inView = 'undefined'). Neither value is constant, so a one-time body class goes stale.
corr:
The finding is right. Two refinements:
- Item 86 (QUEUE.md:1323-1352) already gives `loopWhileVisible`, which pauses looping animations with `.mo-off` while an element is off screen or the page is hidden. The handoff's own `fw-paused` should map onto that, or be replaced by it.
- Following the handoff text is not a guaranteed audit failure. Gating on `motionOK()` would actually satisfy the "nothing moves before the first tap" rule. The real problem is that it does not match how item 87 treats ambient loops and leaves fred frozen until the first tap. Whether the world should move before a tap is Mark's call. The app's precedent (sky loops, item 87) says yes, through ON_LOAD_OK.

The problem is real, but one point needs care. Item 85's rule is "no motion on plain page load", and `motionOK()` is built to keep things still until the first tap. So keeping the world still until the first tap would follow that rule; only the life the handoff asks for would be lost. Letting the loops run from load has a precedent (item 87's sky loops), but each loop then has to be added to ON_LOAD_OK under items 97-99 with its reason, and Mark should approve that, because it widens what item 85 allows. Either way, the app script has to toggle `body.anim` itself. It should do so on the Reduce Motion matchMedia change listener, on a `worldMotion` settings change and, if the tap gate is kept, on the first trusted tap. One test at load is not enough. Off-screen and background pausing should use `loopWhileVisible` / `.mo-off` rather than a separate `fw-paused` class.

The staleness problem is real; calling motionOK() "the wrong gate" is a design choice, not a bug. motionOK() is Mark's item-85 rule ("nothing moves before the rider's first tap or key", index.html:8719), and the audit enforces it: before the first tap nothing may move except what ON_LOAD_OK lists. Gating the crew on motionOK() is therefore the conservative choice that passes the audit with no exception added. Running the crew from load with !reducedMotion() like the sky is also valid, but it widens Mark's rule. It needs his OK and an ON_LOAD_OK entry under item 97/98/99, and the review should ask him rather than assume. Either way the fix is the same: re-evaluate body.anim whenever the inputs change. That means on the first trusted pointerdown/keydown (the same listener as index.html:8834), on the prefers-reduced-motion matchMedia change, and on a settings.worldMotion change. For pausing, use loopWhileVisible/.mo-off rather than the bundle's own fw-paused.

title: The bundle's fw-paused pause misses most scene loops; the app's .mo-off pauses all of them
rec: Do not use fw-paused or a second observer in the app. Call loopWhileVisible(el) on each sky card, weather sky, crew strip and Journal world. That is item 86's pattern, and it also covers document.hidden. Drop the 'fw-paused off screen' line from item 97, or say it is replaced by .mo-off.
ev: Probe with body.anim and a host holding FW.scene, a bird and wxSky('snow'): 123 animations running. Adding fw-paused to the host still leaves 46 running (tw, drift, fw-shafts, swag, fog, ch-pump, float, hs, hover, sway…). The scene rule is `.scene.fw-paused *`, which only matches when the class is on .scene itself, and cast.css lists only a few parts under `.fw-paused`. The app's `.mo-off` (index.html:6098-6099, in @layer mo-off, !important) on the same host pauses all 108 of 108, including the !important fw-dance (probe2.txt: before 108, moOff 0). review.html:252 uses its own IntersectionObserver with fw-paused.
corr:
What does hold, at low severity:
1. **Scene rule needs the class on `.scene` itself.** `.scene.fw-paused *` (fred-world.css:162) only works when fw-paused is on the .scene element itself. The cast and weather rules work from any ancestor. A fw-paused on a parent card above .scene leaves about 80 scene loops running.
2. **The review page has this bug.** review.html:252-253 puts fw-paused on .rv-stage, a parent of .scene, so its own off-screen pause misses the scene loops. That only affects the design review page, not the app.
3. **Item 97 wording is inconsistent.** Its line "`fw-paused` off screen and in background" disagrees with HANDOFF.md:66 ("pause with the item-86 pattern").

The recommendation still stands as a clean-up: in item 97, say the app pauses with loopWhileVisible(el) (.mo-off, which also covers document.hidden) on each sky, crew strip and Journal world, and does not use fw-paused or a second observer.

The finding overstates one thing. fw-paused does pause every scene loop when it is on the .scene wrapper itself, which HANDOFF line 78 tells hosts to add as <div class="scene" data-sky=…>. My probe confirms this: 0 loops running with fw-paused on .scene plus the host. The finding's probe never had a .scene element, because FW.scene() returns only the SVG. So the real defect is narrower: an fw-paused class on any ancestor (a card, body, or the review page's root) misses the scene loops, while the cast and weather loops do pause from an ancestor. That inconsistency is a trap, and review.html falls into it. The recommendation still holds: item 97 should say to call loopWhileVisible(el) on each sky card, weather sky, crew strip and Journal world (the item-86 pattern, which also covers document.hidden) instead of using fw-paused or a second IntersectionObserver. Severity is closer to low-to-medium: loops would keep running off screen (a performance cost), but nothing breaks.

The finding is correct, with two small refinements. First, the probe count is 45 still running, not 46. Second, the `.scene.fw-paused *` rule is dead code rather than simply too narrow: the scene's root has the class `world`, and no `.scene` element exists, so the rule cannot match even when fw-paused is put on the scene itself. Also, HANDOFF.md:66 already points to the item-86 pattern, so the fix is to make line 94 agree with it: drop the fw-paused line in favour of loopWhileVisible / .mo-off. The bundle's fw-paused rules should also be fixed or removed so nobody relies on them.

title: fw-dance keeps dancing under Reduce Motion while body.anim is on
rec: Ask the design chat to remove the !important, or to raise the reduced-motion rule to `.anim .fw-dance .ch`. In the app, keep anim off body whenever reducedMotion() is true (as in the finding above), which also covers this.
ev: fred-world.css: `.anim .fw-dance .ch{animation:fw-dance 4s ease-in-out infinite!important}` has specificity (0,3,0). The bundle's own `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.fw-dance .ch{animation:none!important}}` is (0,2,0) and the app's `*{animation:none!important}` is (0,0,0), so both lose. Probe with Reduce Motion emulated and body.anim on: 1 animation still running, 'fw-dance ch' (probe.txt reduce.runningUnderAnim=1). This contradicts the handoff's claim that 'The CSS also honours prefers-reduced-motion'.
corr: The defect is real but narrower than stated. HANDOFF.md:66 and :94 already say to put `anim` on body only when `motionOK()`. In origin/main index.html:8725, `motionOK()` returns `MOV.live && !reducedMotion()`. Built as written, body.anim is therefore never on when the page starts under Reduce Motion. The leak shows up in one case: Reduce Motion is switched on while the page is open and body.anim was already set. It also shows up if the app ever sets anim without checking motionOK. Severity is low to medium, not a clear medium. There are two fixes. In the bundle, drop the !important or make the reduced-motion rule `.anim .fw-dance .ch`. In the app, add a matchMedia change listener that removes `anim` (or adds `rm`) when Reduce Motion turns on, the same pattern as index.html:8987 and :14050. I did not repeat the reviewer's probe myself.

Severity should be low (polish or defence in depth), not medium. The CSS claim is correct: the `.anim .fw-dance .ch` rule with !important beats both the bundle's reduced-motion rule and the app's global one. But the planned integration sets body.anim only when motionOK(), and motionOK() already excludes reducedMotion() (index.html:8725). So users with Reduce Motion on will not see the dance unless the setting changes mid-session without a re-check. Recommendation: ask the design chat to drop the !important or to scope the reduced-motion rule as `.anim .fw-dance .ch`, and fix the wording in HANDOFF.md:66. In item 97, re-run the body.anim toggle on the prefers-reduced-motion change event.

The CSS defect is real, but it only shows up if the app breaks the handoff's own instructions. title: The motion audit fails 55 checks as soon as the CSS is inlined
rec: Item 97 must update kit2/motion KEYFRAMES (and ON_LOAD_OK for loops that play before a tap) for all 55 names with their selectors and items. A practical option: a KEYFRAMES rule that accepts any keyframe defined between the fred-world markers, judged by its selectors under `.anim`. Either way, budget it into item 97; the plan does not mention it.
ev: motion.test.mjs on fwprobe/nfw/null.html (698 s): FAIL 56. That is 55 × 'static unplaced: @keyframes …' (ch-bob, ch-blink, tw, drift, fog, hover, sway, wx-*, hol-*, fw-*, l-in …) plus the static summary line. Every runtime check passed, since nothing renders FW yet (output in review/code/motion.txt). Every rule that runs one of these keyframes must also be listed in KEYFRAMES[n].sel (motion.test.mjs:211-213), so each of the bundle's ~66 `.anim …` selectors has to be listed. The bundle adds 55 keyframes and no name clashes with main's 34.
corr: Correct as stated: 55 new keyframes, each fails as "unplaced", and none clashes with main's names. One small addition: once a name is added to KEYFRAMES, the check at motion.test.mjs:207-213 still fails until every rule that runs it is listed in KEYFRAMES[n].sel. That check is a source scan, so it fails even when nothing renders FW. Item 97 should budget for the kit2/motion KEYFRAMES and ON_LOAD_OK update, or for a marker-scoped rule. Unverified: the count of about 66 selectors.

The selector count is understated. I counted 82 CSS rules in fred-world.css that set animation or animation-name, covering 133 comma-separated selectors, not about 66. Some of these may be Reduce Motion or paused overrides that set animation:none; I did not check that. The fix is bigger than adding 55 names: KEYFRAMES[n].sel must list every selector that runs each keyframe. ON_LOAD_OK (motion.test.mjs:106-114) also needs entries for every loop that plays before the first tap, such as the sky card and fred bobbing. Each of those entries needs a QUEUE item number, because item 85 bans motion on plain page load unless it is listed. I did not re-run the audit myself; this rests on the existing motion.txt output and on reading the code.

This is not a defect in the bundle. The audit is doing its job and flagging animations nobody has placed yet. The real gap is that item 97 does not budget for the work. Severity is medium at most and arguably low: the work is a bookkeeping change to the kit, not a break in the app. Two parts of the finding are guesses, not facts. First, the claim that all 55 need ON_LOAD_OK is unverified: only loops that play before the first tap need it, which should be the sky, fred's idle and the crew. Second, the "accept anything between the markers" rule is only a suggestion. It would also weaken the rule Mark's audit enforces, where each animation is placed with its QUEUE item. Listing each keyframe under item 97-103 as it goes live fits the kit's design better.

area: B5 / B2 performance advice, inventory audit
title: A cached art string inserted twice duplicates SVG ids and breaks the rim light
rec: Cache per instance, not per string. Alternatively, have the bundle accept an id prefix (as scene(id) does) or number ids with a counter. Do not reuse a string across screens.
ev: bird/person/bike/kitty build their def ids with Math.random (fred-world.js:43, 97, 433, 463). The same FW.bird() string inserted twice gives 2 duplicate ids (probe.txt cachedTwiceDupIds=2). When the first copy is hidden (display:none, as in an inactive view), the visible copy's url(#…) masks resolve to the hidden defs. Screenshot review/code/cached-twice-motion.png: the left bird (cached string) shows a grey edge where the right bird (fresh call) shows the lit rim. The inventory audit also fails on 'an id used by two elements in one document'.
corr: Narrowing: the visible damage only happens when the first copy in the document is inside a display:none subtree. If two copies of the same string are both visible, they render correctly in Chromium, although the duplicate ids are still invalid and will still fail the inventory audit. WebKit/iOS is unverified. The finding also understates one point: the handoff itself tells us to cache the string (B2, HANDOFF.md:54). So the advice to fix is "cache the string": cache per screen or per instance, or have the bundle take an id prefix or use a counter.

Mostly right. One limit on scope: it only happens when the same cached string is in the document twice at the same time, for example on two views that both stay in the DOM. Re-rendering one screen by replacing its innerHTML is safe. Caching per screen or per element, or giving each copy its own id prefix or counter, fixes it. Medium severity is fair, since the result is visible rendering damage and not data loss.

Everything else in the finding is correct. Only the wording of the alternative fix needs changing: scene's signature is scene(p, season), where p is an id prefix used for all of its defs (`${p}sky`, `${p}fog`, and so on). The fix is to give bird/person/kitty/bike an optional prefix option of the same kind, or a counter, instead of Math.random. Or cache per instance: never insert one cached cast string in two places in the document at once.
notes: REAL: I tried to refute this and could not. It holds in Chromium. The ids come from Math.random in FW.bird, FW.person, the kitty and the bike/chalk figure (fred-world.js:43, 97, 433, 463). In my run one FW.bird({wear:['beanie']}) string had 2 ids (bqo6pa and bqo6par), and its url(#…) references point at them. title: Random SVG ids will defeat the inventory baseline
rec: Use deterministic ids (a counter, or a prefix the caller passes). Otherwise add an allow.json entry with a regex for the FW id shapes and a stated reason.
ev: inventory.mjs records every element id and reports any baseline id that is gone. It turns digit runs into # and replaces only localStorage record ids (inventory.mjs header). Ids such as 'b'+Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,7) change on every load. Once a screen with FW art is in baseline-main.json, every later run will report those ids as gone.
corr: The finding is correct as written. One addition: the scene builder's ${p} prefix (fred-world.js lines 561-567) should be checked for the same problem before relying on a regex allow entry. A deterministic counter or a prefix the caller passes is the cleaner fix, because a regex that also has to cover the letters in the random part (for example ^[bpkc][a-z0-9#]{1,5}(c|g|f|b|h|k|chk)?$) is broad and could hide real losses.

One detail in the evidence is wrong. Element ids are not digit-normalised: only texts, data-* values and accessible names go through norm() (lines 154, 175-196). Ids get deRec() only, and the looks-generated-so-becomes-* rule at line 153 also covers data-* values only. This makes the finding stronger: no part of the id path absorbs a random base-36 suffix. Also, this does not fail yet. FW is not on main, so a branch adding FW art only adds ids against the current baseline, which is not a loss. The failures start after the merge, once the baseline is re-snapped with FW art in it. One more point: the 11 ids are on clipPath/gradient defs (not controls), so they matter only in the ids list. The fix should either use ids from a counter or caller-passed prefix (stable per render order), or add an allow.json ids entry with a regex for the four prefixes plus the suffix letters, and a why.

Mostly right. Two details to add. First, the ids carry suffixes such as b, c, chk, f, g, h and k, so an allow regex would need to cover shapes like ^[bpkc][a-z#]{1,5}(b|c|chk|f|g|h|k)?$, and a pattern that loose could also hide real losses. That makes deterministic ids (a module counter, or a prefix the caller passes) clearly the better fix. Second, sometimes all five random characters are digits, which normalise to 'b#'. Such an id stays stable, but that is rare and does not change the conclusion.
notes:
REAL: This holds when checked against the code. In /Users/markmccabe/Downloads/handoff/fred-world.js, four art builders make their SVG id prefix from Math.random(): line 43 ('b'), line 97 ('p'), line 433 ('k') and line 463 ('c'), each followed by .toString(36).slice(2,7). Those prefixes then name clipPath, mask, linearGradient and pattern ids, for example lines 16, 28, 49, 65, 178-180 and 477. A new prefix is drawn on every call, so on every page load.

kit2/inventory/inventory.mjs collects ids at line 164 with querySelectorAll('[id]') over the whole document, shown or hidden, so SVG defs ids count. deRec at line 165 normalises them as the header (lines 12-14) says: digit runs become #, and only saved localStorage record ids of 5 or more characters become *. A random base-36 id such as 'bk3f9a' becomes 'bk#f#a', which still differs from load to load. Under the header's rule (line 17), an id in the baseline that appears on no screen afterwards is reported as GONE.

So once a screen showing FW art is snapped into baseline-main.json, every later run will report those ids as gone unless allow.json has an entry for them. The timing in the finding is also right. The current baseline is main without FW, and new ids are never counted as losses, so the problem starts only after the item merges and main is snapped again. Severity low is fair: it affects the test harness, not users.

Users who have not entered a birthday simply do not get the birthday look; a link to the existing field is enough, in the way races already link to it at 15122 (`profileReveal('birthday','pBirthday')`).

Mostly right; four details need fixing.
(1) The count is off. `settings.birthday` appears 13 times in origin/main, not 18; "birthday" appears more often if you count all uses.
(2) "The app has no profile object" is not quite true. Sync writes `data.profile={displayName, photoURL, email}` from the Google user on every push (index.html:17591). So a `profile.birthday` placed there would be rebuilt from the Google account and lost on each push. That is another reason to use settings.birthday.
(3) The Birthday hint at index.html:6736 says it is "For your race age group, percentile labels and finding your results". If it will also drive the birthday look, that text should say so. That is the right place for the Settings note the finding asks for.
(4) The holidays.js:57 copy ("Needs a birthday field" / "the profile needs a birthday first") should change to read settings.birthday, using the month and day of today's date.

title: Many generic class names are still unprefixed
rec: Ask the design chat to prefix every class with fw- (including anim → fw-anim and rm → fw-rm) and the unprefixed keyframes (tw, drift, fog, float, sway, hover, hs, wob, swag, l-in) before item 97. That keeps the kit's KEYFRAMES list readable and protects against future collisions.
ev: An exact token comparison against every class in index.html (class attributes, classList calls and CSS) finds only `fl` and `p` shared today. Their app rules `.mst-tbar.fl` and `.gp-sq.p` need app classes, so nothing leaks either way. The app's `.ch-head .rs-eyebrow` needs .rs-eyebrow, so it does not touch the bundle's ch-head. Even so, the bundle styles the bare names anim, rm, scene, sun, fog, tw, hover, stalk, bird, deco, fl, fall, burst, cheer, waves, world, phone, enter, p1-p3 and vm1-vm5. `.cheer` and `.scene` are styled without needing any ancestor. corr: "Contradicts the handoff" goes too far. HANDOFF.md:47 only says that classes which clashed were renamed fw-*. That is literally true: nothing clashes with index.html today. The real point is that this is fragile. Many bare names are global, and with anim on body, a future app class named sun, fog, tw, hover, stalk, cheer or scene would pick up the bundle's styles or animations. Also, `rm` is a documented API class (HANDOFF.md:66), so renaming anim and rm means changing the handoff text and the item 97 steps too, not just the CSS.

The recommendation still stands: ask for an fw- prefix on the generic classes and keyframes, with anim and rm the most important because they go on body. The point about the kit's KEYFRAMES list is unverified, since I found no KEYFRAMES list under /Users/markmccabe/code/fuel-work/kit2/lib.

title: Item 97 needs the next cache number and must add any new icon to SHELL
rec: Inlining needs no SHELL change. Item 97 still bumps CACHE and APP_BUILD together, to v121 if 95 and 96 merge first. A new maskable icon file must be added to SHELL and the manifest with purpose 'maskable'. Do not regenerate icon-192.png as maskable, because apple-touch-icon uses it.
ev: origin/main sw.js has `const CACHE = 'fred-shell-v118'` and index.html:9083 has APP_BUILD = v118. The unmerged q95-small is at v119 and q96-sync at v120. SHELL lists ./icon-192.png and ./icon-512.png. manifest.webmanifest has no maskable entry, and apple-touch-icon uses icon-192.png (index.html:14).
corr: Small nuance: whether item 97 lands on v119, v120 or v121 depends on how many of items 95 and 96 merge first. The rule to follow is "next number after whatever main holds, and CACHE equals APP_BUILD", not a fixed v121.

Two small points. A new maskable file only has to be in SHELL to be available offline on first load. The icons themselves would still work without it, so this is offline completeness, not breakage. The version number also depends on merge order: it is v121 only if both 95 and 96 merge first. Otherwise it is the next number after whatever is on main when 97 merges.

The finding stands. One detail to add: CACHE and APP_BUILD must stay equal, because the kit checks them (index.html:9083 comment). The number will be v121 only if both 95 and 96 merge first. Otherwise it is the next number after whatever main holds at merge time.

title: The fw-flow keyframes animate stroke-dashoffset, outside 'only transform and opacity'
rec: Either accept it with the same reason the app's rwx-frost has, or replace the dash flow with a translate.
ev: In the bundle's 55 keyframes, every property is transform or opacity except fw-flow: ['stroke-dashoffset']. The kit's LAYOUT regex does not flag it, and the app does the same in rwx-frost and the graffiti, but the handoff says 'Only transform and opacity animate'.
corr: The precedent the recommendation leans on is weaker than it sounds. The app's rwx-frost and gf-draw are one-shot draw-ons (`forwards`, 2.6 s and 1.4 s) that stop after they play once. fw-flow is an infinite loop that repaints the stroke every 0.6 s for as long as it is on screen. A 0.6 s loop also breaks the handoff's own rule on the same line (HANDOFF.md:44) that loops nest in 1/2/4/20 s. QUEUE.md:1267 allows only "transform and opacity, plus bar widths", which does not cover dashoffset loops. So "accept it for the same reason as rwx-frost" does not really hold. The better fix is to replace the dash flow with a translate or opacity step on a 1 s loop, or to make it a one-shot. If Mark wants to keep it, the decision should be logged as an exception.

The precedent the finding cites is weaker than it says. The app's rwx-frost (index.html:5440, 5460) and the gf-draw graffiti (index.html:3580-3584) are both one-shot draw-ins that stop (`forwards`). rwx-frost is also allowed in the spec by name (QUEUE.md:1395, "stroke-dashoffset 1 → 0 over 2.6 s, once"). fw-flow is different: it loops forever (infinite), so the stroke repaints every frame while it is on screen. Its 0.6 s period also breaks the same HANDOFF.md:44 rule that loops nest in 1/2/4/20 s. So "accept it for the same reason as rwx-frost" does not hold up. Better fix: replace the dash flow with a translate or opacity loop at a 1 s period. If it stays, add a written exception to the spec.

The finding holds, and one detail makes it stronger. fw-flow is an infinite 0.6 s loop. That goes against two rules on HANDOFF.md:44: only transform and opacity animate, and loops nest in 1/2/4/20 s. The app's rwx-frost precedent is only partly comparable, because it runs once and stops (`forwards`) rather than looping. A better fix than accepting the precedent is to animate a translate on a patterned or clipped stroke, or to slow it to a nested loop length, and to keep it behind the `.anim` / Reduce Motion gate.

title: profile.birthday ("MM-DD") duplicates the existing settings.birthday and would be wiped in the cloud
rec: Drop profile.birthday from section E and remove 'add a birthday field' from item 103. Show the birthday look when settings.birthday.slice(5) equals today's MM-DD, and use Feb 28 in non-leap years for Feb 29 birthdays. If Mark wants a month-and-day-only option, that's a separate change because age groups need the year.
ev: origin/main index.html:7885 DEFAULT_SETTINGS already has birthday:''; :8612 and :14581 validate it as YYYY-MM-DD; :6734 <input id="pBirthday" type="date" autocomplete="bday"> in Settings › Profile › Birthday; :17357 saves it. It is used for race age groups (:15044, :15058), sent in the races AI prompt as BIRTH_DATE (:9065), dropped from the troubleshooting copy (:9087-9088) and kept on restore (:14572, :14580). The app has no local 'profile' object. The only 'profile' is the cloud field users/{uid}.profile, which syncOps replaces whole on every sign-in write: :17591 data.profile={displayName, photoURL, email} with mergeFields 'profile'. A profile.birthday written there would be erased.
corr: Severity is arguable. Nothing breaks today, but building item 103 as written would duplicate a field users already fill in, and a cloud write could erase the new one. The recommendation stands: use settings.birthday, compare its MM-DD part (`.slice(5)`) with today's date, and treat Feb 29 as Feb 28 in non-leap years. Item 103 and section E do not need a new field.

The duplicate field and the clash with existing code are confirmed. Two points should be softened. (1) The cloud wipe only happens if a builder literally puts the field at users/{uid}.profile. Section E also says "All sync like other settings", so a builder could just as easily add a second key, settings.profile.birthday or an MM-DD settings field. That would not be wiped, but it would duplicate and conflict with the existing settings.birthday, which has to stay YYYY-MM-DD or :8612 and :14581 clear it. (2) Because the wipe is conditional and no data is lost today, this is a plan step that will not work as written: medium, or high only if built against the cloud profile field. The recommendation stands. Drop profile.birthday from section E and the "add a birthday field" step from item 103. Show the birthday look when settings.birthday.slice(5) equals today's MM-DD, and use Feb 28 in non-leap years for Feb 29 birthdays. Also change the bundle's holiday text at fred-world.js:753 ('Needs a birthday field' / 'the profile needs a birthday first') so it points to Settings › Profile › Birthday. That text can only be changed in the source and rebuilt, not hand-edited.

The finding holds, with one change to severity. The erasure only happens if someone builds profile.birthday as written, as a cloud users/{uid}.profile field. Anyone building item 103 would likely spot the existing Settings › Profile › Birthday field first. So this is better rated medium (a plan step that won't work as written, plus a duplicate field) than high. Real data loss needs that literal build. title: New settings keys filled in from DEFAULT_SETTINGS get stamped on an unrelated save and overwrite another device's choice (item 96)
rec: Don't add rider, crew, holidayThemes or worldMotion to DEFAULT_SETTINGS. Read them with fallbacks (settings.rider || FW.RIDER_DEFAULT, settings.crew?.show !== false, ...) and write them only on an explicit edit. Or harden sfNote so a key missing from prev whose value equals DEFAULT_SETTINGS[k] is not stamped. Add a two-device kit case (kit2/q91 fbmock): A sets a rider, B (not pulled) saves an unrelated setting, both pull, A's rider stands.
ev: wt-q96 index.html:8555 settings=Object.assign({}, DEFAULT_SETTINGS, load(...)); :17580-17582 syncBeforeSave compares localStorage (prev) to the new value; :17527 sfNote stamps every key that differs. A key that exists only as an in-memory default therefore gets stamped with the time of the first save of any setting. Simulation (scratchpad/review/data/sfsim.mjs, which runs q96 lines 17514-17539 as-is): device A uploads a custom rider at t=1000. Device B upgrades, hasn't pulled yet, and changes another setting at t=2000. Result: B's stamps {kit:2000, rider:2000}, merged rider = the default {kit:'#179BCC'}, keys to upload ['kit','rider']. The user's custom rider is replaced on every device. The same applies to crew, holidayThemes and worldMotion: a switch flipped on one device gets reverted.
corr: The mechanism is right, but it only happens under certain conditions, and the issue sits in q96 rather than in the handoff. (1) Device B must save a setting after upgrading and before its first pull. If B pulls first, sfMerge counts B's unstamped default as 0, the cloud's stamped rider wins, and the result is written to localStorage with SY.applying set, so later saves are safe. Realistic cases are a phone used offline, or an edit made before the boot pull finishes. In the bad case, though, the default really is uploaded and replaces the custom rider on every device. (2) HANDOFF.md does not say to add these keys to DEFAULT_SETTINGS. This is a trap in the build, not something the plan states. (3) It is a latent property of item 96 that any future DEFAULT_SETTINGS key will hit (key-by-key stamps were new in q96). The better fix is in sfNote: skip a key that is missing from prev and whose value equals DEFAULT_SETTINGS[k]. Alternatively, write the default keys into localStorage before SY.booted. Either fix covers every future default key, so the fred-world keys don't need special-casing. Add the two-device kit case as proposed. Severity: medium-high (it can lose user data, but only under that ordering), not unconditionally high.

Partly conditional. The handoff never says to add these keys to DEFAULT_SETTINGS. The bug appears only if the build puts them there, or writes FW.RIDER_DEFAULT into settings before the user picks anything, and the device then saves before its first pull merges. That happens when it is offline or saves before the boot pull lands. If the pull lands first, the cloud's stamp beats the local key, which has no stamp (it counts as 0), and nothing is lost. The cause is a general q96 trap: any new key added to DEFAULT_SETTINGS is stamped on the first save after an upgrade. It is not a fred-world bug as such. So the right fix is to change sfNote: skip a key that is missing from prev and whose value equals DEFAULT_SETTINGS[k]. Reading the fred-world keys with fallbacks works too. Either fix should come with the two-device test the finding proposes. High severity is fair because a user's custom rider would be lost, though a plan step written to avoid DEFAULT_SETTINGS would sidestep the problem.

The bug is real, but it only happens in a narrower window than "B hasn't pulled yet" suggests.

After any pull that applies settings, syncSetSettings (:17706) rebuilds settings from DEFAULT_SETTINGS and saves the whole object to localStorage, defaults included. After that, prev contains the new keys and they are no longer stamped by mistake.

On an online, signed-in device the first pull after the upgrade always applies settings. The merged result never contains the in-memory default (the cloud's value wins, or the key drops out because the cloud lacks it), so it differs from local settings and gets saved. The exposure is therefore the first settings save after the upgrade that lands before the first successful pull. That happens when:
- the device opens offline,
- the pull fails, or
- the device is signed out or has sync off and signs in later, since stamps accrue in the meantime (the item 95 path).

In that window it does silently replace a rider, crew or holiday/motion choice made on another device, so high (user data) is defensible, though medium-high is fairer given how narrow the window is.

The same flaw applies to any key added to DEFAULT_SETTINGS in future, not only the fred world keys. The general fix is better: harden sfNote so a key missing from prev whose new value equals DEFAULT_SETTINGS[k] gets no stamp, or save settings once at startup before SY.booted. Keep the proposed two-device kit test.

title: settings.rider is put into SVG markup without validation (markup injection via a backup file or the synced doc)
rec: Add riderNorm(r) to the app: each key must be one of FW.RIDER_OPTIONS (hex colours from the lists, enums from the maps), otherwise RIDER_DEFAULT. Call it on load (next to :8612), in restoreAll, and when synced settings are applied. Ideally also clamp the values in cast.js riderBase and rebuild.

Probe scratchpad/review/data/xss.mjs: FW.riderAvatar({kit:'red"/>'}) and FW.riderOutfit(...) both return output containing the markup. corr: Correct as stated. One refinement: this is a gap in item 100 as planned, not in the current app, because main has no settings.rider yet. The fix the finding recommends is the right one. Check each key against FW.RIDER_OPTIONS; frame has no options list, so it needs a hex regex or must be '#fff'. Do this on load, in restoreAll after the Object.assign at :14575, and where synced settings are applied, or alternatively clamp inside cast.js riderBase and rebuild the bundle.

The mechanism holds, but the risk is narrower than the finding suggests. settings.rider does not exist in the app yet; item 100 adds it, so this is a gap in the plan, not a bug in main. The 'synced doc' route needs someone who can already write to the user's own Firestore document. The realistic route is a crafted backup file that the user picks and confirms. That makes it defense-in-depth or self-XSS, which sits between medium and low. The fix is still right and cheap: a riderNorm(r) that keeps only values from FW.RIDER_OPTIONS and otherwise uses RIDER_DEFAULT. title: Restoring an older backup loses the user's rider and the new switches
rec: Extend the keep-this-device's pattern to rider, crew, holidayThemes and worldMotion, run riderNorm on the restored rider, and add a test with a pre-100 backup.
ev: main :14575 settings=Object.assign({}, DEFAULT_SETTINGS, d.settings). Every backup made before item 100 lacks rider, crew, holidayThemes and worldMotion, so restoring one resets them to defaults or deletes them.
corr: The real loss is the rider: a user-built look is replaced by the default. crew, holidayThemes and worldMotion only fall back to their defaults (show on, names off, themes on, motion on), so the user loses a switch change, not data. Medium fits the rider; the switches are low. The fix as recommended still stands. In restoreAll, keep this device's rider, crew, holidayThemes and worldMotion when the backup has no such key, the same way it already does for birthday, gender and the others. Run riderNorm (or whatever normalizer item 100 adds) on the result. Add a test that restores a backup made before item 100. Also add this rule to item 100's text in QUEUE.md, because section E of the handoff does not mention backup.

The core claim holds, with three refinements.

1. The keep-this-device's pattern is used for fields added after backups already existed. It is not a rule for every setting: most older settings, such as meds, units and heat thresholds, simply take the backup's value or the default. The restore prompt also says the profile is 'replaced by the backup's'.
2. The line references are slightly off. Weight is restored at 14577, myBottles and bottleAsk at 14578, raceName at 14579, and birthday and gender at 14580.
3. The real loss is settings.rider, the avatar the user built. crew, holidayThemes and worldMotion would only fall back to their defaults (crew shown with names off, the other two on). So the user loses changed preferences, not data, and that part is low severity. The medium rating fits only the rider.

The recommendation stands: in restoreAll, keep this device's rider, crew, holidayThemes and worldMotion when d.settings lacks the key; run riderNorm on the rider afterwards; and add a test that restores a backup made before item 100.

The real loss is settings.rider, which the user builds by hand. title: FW.HOLIDAYS has no dates and no ids: the whole date table, including the lunar and lunisolar dates, falls to the app
rec: In item 103, key the table by id. Fixed and nth-weekday days and Easter (Computus) are computed. Lunar New Year, Diwali, Hanukkah and Eid come from a table for 5 years with the source cited in QUEUE_LOG, plus a test that fails when the table has less than 12 months left. Decide in the queue text whether 'Eid' means al-Fitr, al-Adha or both. Use a simple window for the Tour (or drop 'mountains'), and drop Kona/Indy/Bike to Work unless a date source is named. Hanukkah runs from the evening of its first day.
ev: Node probe of the bundle: HOLIDAYS = 3 groups, [title, items] (12 / 4 / 9 = 25 looks). Item keys are only n, w, wear, champ, sky, deco, pick, c, care, col: no id, no rule, no dates. corr: Three corrections. First, leaving the date table to the app is intended, not a gap. title: Overlap rules are missing: the KOM takeover hides Lunar New Year, Valentine's and January–March birthdays every year

Four parts of the finding are overstated.

1. **"Hides":** the plan doesn't say the takeover hides holiday looks. It leaves the case open, because fred still peeks and nothing says whether he wears the look. Kitty can't wear one, since kitty() has no wear option. This is a gap in the spec, not a stated rule that hides them.
2. **Birthdays:** Jan 2–4 is the chase phase, and fred is still shown there (worried, on his bike). So only birthdays from Jan 5 to Mar 6 are affected, not "Jan 2–Mar 6".
3. **Memorial Day and Indy 500:** the race is on Sunday and Memorial Day is the Monday after (I computed 2027: May 30 and May 31). The recommendation stands: put a precedence order in item 103, decide whether the peeking fred wears the day's look or whether kitty() gets a wear option, and add tests for the overlaps.

title: Items 100, 103 and 104 depend on q96, which isn't merged
rec: Merge q95 and q96 before item 97, then build the new keys against sfMerge/sfNote and add the new-key two-device test to the q96 kit section.
ev: git status: q95-small and q96-sync are built but not on origin/main. The main sync is still whole-doc (main :17574-17583 syncMergeDocs), so the new keys behave differently before and after q96 lands.
corr: "Build the new keys against sfMerge/sfNote" needs no special code. q96's sfNote and sfKeys work on any top-level settings key, so once q96 is merged, rider, crew, holidayThemes and worldMotion are stamped and merged key by key with no new sync code. birthday lives in settings.profile, so it syncs as part of that one profile unit, not as a key of its own. The real dependency is merge order: merge q95 and q96 to main before starting item 97. Then add a two-device test (device B changes settings.rider, device A saves something else without pulling first, and B's rider survives) to the q96 sync tests in kit2.

The recommendation is slightly off. The new keys do not need to be "built against sfMerge/sfNote". In q96-sync (index.html:17505-17545), stamping and merging cover every top-level settings key automatically: sfKeys collects any key except updatedAt, schemaVersion and _u. So settings.rider, crew, holidayThemes and worldMotion get per-key sync for free, as long as items 100, 103 and 104 save through the normal settings save path and do not write settings around it. The one real choice is where the birthday goes: if it is nested in settings.profile, it merges together with the rest of the profile, not as its own key. The real fix is simply to merge q95 and q96 first, then add the new-key two-device test to the q96 kit section, as the finding suggests. The items do not strictly depend on q96, since they would still work under whole-doc sync, just with the older stale-upload risk.

It is an ordering point, not a hard dependency. In q96-sync, the per-key merge is generic over every top-level settings key. `sfKeys`, `sfNote` (q96 index.html:17527) and `sfMerge` (:17530) stamp and merge any key that changes, and they have no key registry. New keys therefore need no code written "against sfMerge/sfNote": on main they merge whole-doc like every other key today, and after q96 they merge per key automatically. Two things remain worth doing: (1) merge q95 and q96 before item 97 so the new items build on the base that will ship; (2) add a two-device test for one new key (for example `rider`) to the q96 kit section.

One part needs fixing. `profile.birthday` (item 103) is not a settings key. On main, the only `profile` that syncs is the cloud field `data.profile={displayName, photoURL, email}`, rebuilt from the auth user on every sync (origin/main index.html:17591). A birthday stored there would not sync as a setting, and the next sync would drop it. It should go under settings, for example `settings.birthday`, so it gets the item 96 per-key merge.
notes: REAL: I checked this and it holds. In git, `merge-base --is-ancestor` reports that neither q95-small nor q96-sync is in origin/main. On origin/main, `syncMergeDocs` (index.html about lines 17574-17583) still merges settings as one doc: the newest updatedAt wins the whole doc, with only the dfcGuard, bikeTombMerge and jhpDocMerge guards on top. HANDOFF.md section E puts every new key under settings: settings.rider (item 100), settings.crew, settings.holidayThemes and settings.worldMotion (item 104), and profile.birthday (item 103), and says "All sync like other settings (respect item 96)". title: The Option C sky card has a fixed height and clips its own reading at 200% text (and already at 390 in the review)
rec: Use min-height instead of a fixed height, and keep the reading in normal flow (fred absolutely positioned on the right). At large text, drop fred below the reading or hide him. Add a kit check at 320 px and 200% that the reading is fully visible.

Injected into the app at 320 px with 200% root text: reading scrollHeight 236 px in a 132 px card, so 104 px is cut off (review/product/inj-sky-320x2.png). In review.html at 390 the last words 'for it' are cut (review/product/rv-front-c.png). The brand guide p.27 says text must be 'readable at 200% text size and 320 px wide'.

That card's height is set by the review page's mock layout (review.html has its own .fw-wx overrides, for example line 113, height:120px). The 390 px clip at 100% text is therefore a review-page result, not proof that the shipped card clips at 390. In the shipped CSS at 132 px the reading just fits at 320 and 390 with default text, and it fails badly at 200%. The fix holds either way: use min-height, keep the reading in normal flow, and add a kit check at 320 px with 200% text.

Two details are off, but they don't change the verdict. Second, how much gets cut off depends on the font: about 83 px with the bundle's CSS alone, 104 px in the app. The recommendation is sound: use min-height and keep the reading in normal flow, add a check at 320 px and 200% text, and shorten the Option C line or let it wrap.

"Already at 390" holds only for review.html's own rendering, where the reading is larger. Also add a kit check at 320px with scale 2.

title: The front-page sky card needs a forecast before Crunch, which the app never fetches today
rec: Spell out in item 99: when to fetch (on Plan open? on each ticket change? reuse wxKey and the one-hour cache), what the card shows while loading, offline or with no location (hide the card rather than show a fake sky), and add a privacy note that the place is sent to Open-Meteo before the user taps Crunch.
ev: fetchWeather() (index.html:13176) is only called from the Crunch path (index.html:12916, 12922). Without a forecast the app shows 'Couldn't get the forecast… no forecast' (review/product/after-crunch.png). Item 99 says nothing about loading, offline, no location, a date more than 16 days out, a typed temperature, or run mode.
corr:
Some details in the finding are wrong.
(1) The 'no forecast' text in after-crunch.png comes from the test harness having no network, not from the app. On the live site, Crunch gets the forecast. When a fetch fails, the app uses the hour-keyed localStorage cache (wxCacheFind, 13122/13223) before it shows the 'Couldn't get the forecast' note.
(2) 'A date more than 16 days out' is not an open case. Since q44, any date more than 10 days ahead uses typical weather for the date and place from the archive (13194, upcTypicalWx). The spec should reuse that, not invent new handling.
(3) 'A typed temperature' does not exist. Since q31 the plan always uses the forecast, and offline it uses the last forecast's feels-like in #tempF (comment at 12922).
(4) The privacy point is only partly new. The place name typed into Where is already sent to Open-Meteo geocoding as the user types, for suggestions (13040-13047). What would be new before Crunch is the forecast request with coordinates, including 'Use my location' coordinates.
Corrected recommendation: item 99 should say the card calls fetchWeather() (same wxKey and one-hour wxOld cache, q44 typical weather past 10 days, run-distance length) when Plan opens and after ticket edits, debounced. While loading, offline with no cache, or with no place or date, the card is hidden or shows a neutral state with no made-up sky. It should also note that the forecast request now happens before Crunch.

The privacy part of the recommendation is mostly wrong. The place name already goes to Open-Meteo before Crunch: the place field's autocomplete calls geocoding-api.open-meteo.com as the user types (index.html:13040-13047, for 2 or more letters that are not a ZIP). An early fetch would only add a forecast call to the same provider with the coordinates. At most that needs a one-line note that the provider has not changed, not a new privacy disclosure. The rest of the recommendation should stand, tightened. Item 99 should say:
- When to fetch: once the ticket has a place, date and duration, debounced.
- Reuse the existing caches: key on wxKey, and read the persistent wxCacheGet/wxCacheFind store (13117-13122), which has a one-hour expiry (wxOld) and can fill the card offline for a ticket seen before.
- The card must not write to #wxOut, #tempF or wxAccepted. It should share a fetch helper with no side effects instead.
- Hide the card when there is no forecast (still loading, offline with nothing cached, no place, or a date past the forecast range) rather than show a made-up sky.
- Say what happens in run mode. fetchWeather already works out a distance run's length at 13180.

Two parts are overstated. (1) Privacy: place names already go to Open-Meteo before Crunch. The Where field's live suggestions call geocoding-api.open-meteo.com as the user types (index.html:13047). What would be new is sending the coordinates, date and time to api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast (13190) and the archive (13160) without a tap. The note should cover that, plus Mark's request to send nothing while offline, not "the place". (2) Distant dates and the typed temperature are already handled inside fetchWeather. q44 looks up typical weather from the archive for rides more than ~10 days out (13156-13160), and q31 removed the typed temperature (12922 comment), so item 99 needs only one line on what the card shows for an archive-based "typical" reading. Recommendation: item 99 should call one shared fetch on Plan open and on ticket changes, debounced, reusing wxKey, the one-hour wxOld() rule and the localStorage wx cache. Then the Crunch path can reuse that result. The card should be hidden, not showing a made-up sky, while loading, offline with no cached forecast, or with no place. Run mode also needs a rule.

title: fred's weather outfit doesn't match the closet the app recommends, so 'fred is dressed for it' can contradict the plan
rec: Derive fred's wear from outfit() (map closet ids to bird wear: vest, scarf/arm warmers, beanie, light) instead of the sky kind, and write the HTML line from the same data ('Vest and arm warmers'). The line then carries real information and makes sense to screen-reader users, who can't see the aria-hidden art.
ev: FW.WX[kind].wear: clouds [] (nothing), rain ['umbrella'], night ['vest']. The real closet for the same 52°→55° cloudy ride lists a thermal jersey, vest, arm warmers, leg warmers and toe covers (real/res-closet.png), while the front card says 'Cloudy. fred is dressed for it.' (real/front-c.png) and fred has no extra layers.
corr: Most of this holds, but the mismatch is partly on purpose, and the main fix goes against the design. The handoff splits the two characters on purpose. fred is a weather mascot dressed with props for the sky (style-guide.md:239: "dressed for the weather (umbrella, scarf, sunglasses…)"). The user's own rider is the one who wears "exactly the items outfit() returns" on the Closet card (item 100, HANDOFF.md:111). Dressing fred from outfit() would blur that split, and fred has only 9 wear looks against 34 closet ids. The real fault is the front-card copy: "fred is dressed for it" sounds like clothing advice that fred's art does not give. A better fix keeps fred's sky-based wear and changes the HTML line. Either drop the "dressed for it" claim, or give a short closet summary built from outfit() as text (for example "Thermal jersey, vest, arm warmers"). That also gives screen-reader users real information. Severity is low to medium (copy and polish, nothing breaks), and it only matters in cool skies such as clouds and fog.

Partly right. The mismatch is real, but the design meant fred's look to follow the sky and the rider's look to follow outfit() (item 100), so this is a polish/consistency improvement, between low and medium, and not a defect. The fix as written only partly works. bird() can only show a few weather looks: shades, spritz, beanie, scarf, umbrella, light, sweat, puffs and vest (HANDOFF.md:72). It has no arm warmers, leg warmers, gloves or toe covers, so "scarf for arm warmers" would misrepresent the closet. Better options:
(a) Keep the sky-based look, but add a vest or beanie from outfit() when it recommends a thermal or wind layer.
(b) Change the line so it does not claim fred is dressed for the ride, and use outfit() for the text instead ("Thermal jersey, vest, arm warmers").
(c) Put the user's rider from item 100 in that card instead of fred.
Whichever you pick, building the HTML line from outfit() is the useful part.

Keep the finding, but lower it to low/medium polish and change the recommendation. Driving fred from outfit() undoes the handoff's design: fred shows the sky, and the rider (item 100) shows the closet. It also does not map well, because bird() only has nine weather looks (shades, spritz, beanie, scarf, umbrella, light, sweat, puffs, vest; HANDOFF.md:72). Most closet ids have no match: thermal jersey, arm warmers, leg warmers, gloves and toe covers. Better fix: keep fred's sky look and change the front-card line so it does not claim to describe the outfit. Either write a short closet summary built from outfit() (for example "Thermal jersey, vest, arm and leg warmers"), or drop "fred is dressed for it" and use the forecast line. Optionally, map just the few ids bird() can show (vest, beanie/cap, scarf, light) as extra layers on top of the sky look, so fred is never under-dressed against the closet.

title: Item 103 adds a birthday field that already exists, under a key that would be overwritten in the cloud
rec: Drop 'add a birthday field' and section E's profile.birthday. Read the month and day from settings.birthday, and say in the field's hint that it also shows a birthday look.
ev: The app already has Settings › Birthday (input#pBirthday, index.html:6734) stored as settings.birthday 'YYYY-MM-DD' (index.html:8612), backed up to the account (privAbout, index.html:17999). Every upload writes data.profile={displayName, photoURL, email} (index.html:17591), so a new profile.birthday 'MM-DD' would duplicate the field and be replaced on each upload.
corr: Mostly right. The overwrite happens on sign-in syncs (syncOps called with a user, index.html:17789/17791), not on every upload: the background upload at 17690 passes null and does not touch profile. I would rate it medium rather than high. Section E is ambiguous enough that a builder might store it in settings, and no existing data would be lost. The real harm is a duplicate Birthday field in Settings, plus a birthday look that silently disappears if the value is stored in the cloud profile. The fix stands: drop the new field and section E's profile.birthday, and take the month and day from settings.birthday (slice(5) of 'YYYY-MM-DD'). Then update the Birthday hint at index.html:6736, which today says the field is used only for race age groups and results, so it also mentions the birthday look.

The duplicate is certain, and it is the main problem. The cloud loss happens only if the builder follows the `profile.` prefix literally and writes into users/{uid}.profile. Section E also says these keys "sync like other settings", so a builder who stores it as a setting would get a second, conflicting birthday rather than data loss. Severity is therefore closer to medium than high: as written, the plan step is wrong, but it breaks nothing until someone builds it that way. The fix stays the same: drop the new field and the `profile.birthday` line, take the month and day from `settings.birthday`, and update the Birthday hint (and the 'Needs a birthday field' text in holidays.js) to say it also turns on the birthday look.

The finding holds. Item 103 and section E ask for a birthday field that already exists as settings.birthday ('YYYY-MM-DD', Settings › Profile › Birthday, already synced in the settings doc). The recommendation is right: drop the new field and profile.birthday, and get the month and day for the birthday look from settings.birthday.

Two parts should be scaled back. First, the cloud overwrite only happens if the value goes into the Firestore users/{uid}.profile map: syncOps at index.html:17591 replaces that map on every signed-in upload. Section E says it should sync like other settings, so the likelier result is a duplicate key with a different format, not data loss. Second, severity is closer to medium (a plan step that would duplicate an existing field) than high, unless it is built literally as the cloud profile.birthday.

title: Off switches come last (item 104) while the always-on art ships in items 97-103
rec: Ship each switch with its feature (Animate the world in 97, Show the crew in 99, Holiday themes in 103) and drop 104 as a separate item.
ev: Section A: ship to everyone with no beta switch. Item 104 (Show the crew, Show their names, Holiday themes, Animate the world) is the final item, and each item can take up to 7 review rounds. Until 104 lands, the only way to stop the idle loops is the OS Reduce Motion setting. WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide) asks for a way to stop auto-playing motion that lasts more than 5 s.
corr: The order problem is real, but the WCAG 2.2.2 point overstates how new or how bad it is. The app already ships always-on infinite loops on the weather card's living sky: rwx-glow 5 s, rwx-rays 40 s, rwx-drift 50 s, rwx-fall, rwx-snow and others (origin/main index.html:5458-5467). These have no in-app off switch either, only prefers-reduced-motion. So fred world makes an existing pattern bigger, mostly on the front page in item 99. It is not a new failure that the order causes, and the app does not meet 2.2.2 today with or without fred world. Item 97 alone adds no visible motion ("no visual change except the icon", HANDOFF.md:96), so the gap really starts at 98. Severity is better rated low to medium. The recommendation is still sound: put Animate the world (settings.worldMotion AND-ed with motionOK) in 97 or 98, Show the crew in 99 and Holiday themes in 103, or move 104 to come right after 97. Since the living sky has the same gap, the motion switch could also cover the existing rwx loops.

Downgrade to low (polish/sequencing). This is not a break of any rule in QUEUE.md or the handoff: the app already ships an endless weather-sky loop (item 87) with Reduce Motion as its only stop. A sound suggestion is to ship each switch with its feature: Animate the world and Show the crew with item 99 (or move item 104 to right after 97), Show their names with the crew strip, and Holiday themes with 103. Item 97 needs no switch, because it makes no visible change. Optional: give the world loops a tap-to-pause, or limit how long they run (WCAG 2.2.2). That would be a new rule Mark would need to approve, not an existing one.

Downgrade to a low-severity ordering suggestion, not a problem. Shipping each switch with its feature is still a sensible tidy-up: Animate the world (settings.worldMotion) with 98, the first item that animates (not 97, which has no visible change); Show the crew with 99; Holiday themes with 103. 104 could then shrink to grouping these switches in Settings › Bluebird crew, or be dropped. Until then the interim state matches the app's existing living-sky loops, which stop only under Reduce Motion and pause off screen. It does not break any QUEUE.md rule.

REAL: The ordering fact is right. HANDOFF.md says "Ship to all users (no beta switch)" (line 16). The only in-app switches are in item 104 (lines 124-125), the last item. rec: Write the exception into QUEUE.md. The suggestion to play idle loops for about 6-8 s and then settle (replaying only when the forecast or look changes) is a sensible option to offer. Writing the exception explicitly into QUEUE.md (items 97/99/101) is right either way. Severity: low to medium, a spec clarification rather than a broken rule.
