title: Your rider offers only four light skin tones and three hair styles, and it replaces everyone's avatar
rec: Before item 100 ships: at least 8-10 tones across the full range, more hair options (curly/afro, long, shaved, covered), and a neutral default (or keep the letter or initial until the user builds a rider). Add a 'Use initials' option.
ev: cast.js:89 SKIN = light #F2C4A5, fair #F6D0B8, tan #E2A982, ruddy #F0B79C; RIDER_OPTIONS.hairStyle short/pony/braids (cast.js:366-368). There are no medium-dark or dark tones and no curly, long, shaved or covered styles. Item 100 swaps the header and sidebar avatar for this rider for all users (RIDER_DEFAULT is skin 'light').
corr: The facts hold, but medium fits better than high. Nothing breaks, and it goes against no rule Mark set; it is a visible representation problem in a feature shipping to everyone. Priorities before item 100 ships: (1) more skin tones covering the full range, including medium-brown and dark, each with a shade colour; (2) a neutral default, or keep the initial letter until the user saves a rider (a 'Use initials' option works too); (3) at least one curly or afro hair texture. A 'covered' or 'shaved' style adds little because the rider always wears a helmet (cast.js:382).

Partly overstated. (1) Severity should be medium, not high. It is a visible product and inclusivity problem. It does not break the app, user data, privacy or legal, and it does not break any rule Mark set. (2) Replacing the letter avatar for everyone is Mark's own decision (HANDOFF.md section A, "Your rider" row), not a defect. The fair suggestion is to keep the initial (or a neutral silhouette) until the user saves a rider, or to offer a "Use initials" option. Treat that as a proposal to Mark, not a rule violation. (3) Hair styles matter less than the finding says. riderBase (cast.js:382) always puts a road helmet on the rider (hat:{type:'road'}), so "shaved" or "covered" hair is mostly hidden. Ask for one or two more styles (curly/afro, long), not a full set. The real must-fix before item 100 ships is the skin range: about 8 or more tones, including medium-dark and dark, each with its own shadow shade. A neutral or prompted default should replace the hard-coded 'light' default.

The core claim holds, but I would rate it medium, not high. It is a visible product and inclusiveness problem and a step that should change before item 100 ships. It does not break the app, touch user data or privacy, or break a legal rule. One part of the recommendation needs adjusting. riderBase always puts a road helmet on the rider (cast.js:382: hat type 'road'), so hair mostly peeks out from under it. Adding 'covered' or 'shaved' styles matters less than adding a full range of skin tones (8-10, including medium-dark and dark) plus a 'none' hair option. HANDOFF.md:23 records his final decision that all 25 looks ship, including the five care looks, and HANDOFF.md:125 gives one Holiday themes switch, on by default. The part that clearly holds is the missing acceptance step. The design notes (holidays.js:44, 45, 47) ask that someone who celebrates review the Hanukkah, Diwali and Eid looks, but items 103/104 and the checks in section F have no such step. Add one to 103: a sign-off for each care look, with the Memorial Day "keep it quiet" note followed. rec: Get written permission from Zwift or the KOM party organisers, or replace the Z with a neutral mark (polka dots or a KOM chevron) before Jan 2. Drop the icon swap now: iOS keeps the icon captured at Add to Home Screen (manifest icon-192 at index.html:14), so it can't change at runtime.

rec: Suggested order: 97 (bundle and motion plumbing only) → 98 (weather card fred, smallest visible win) → 100 (rider and closet, after 96 merges) → 99 (front page with its switches) → 103a (holiday table and switch) → 103b (KOM Kitty, only if it can land by Jan 2, otherwise next year) → 101 → 102 → icon last as its own item. Today is Nov 5. Thanksgiving is Nov 26, Hanukkah Dec 4-12, Kitty starts Jan 2, 2027. Items 95 and 96 (per-field settings merge) are built but not merged, and 100, 103 and 104 add synced settings.

Mostly right, with fixes to the details.
(1) Item 97 does not contradict itself. Its acceptance explicitly excepts the icon, so this is a sizing and reversibility argument, not a spec conflict.
(2) The suggested order leaves out item 104. It folds the crew switches into 99 and the holiday switch into 103a without saying so. Also, 99's crew switches (settings.crew) are synced settings too, so 99 also belongs after 96 merges, not just 100.
(3) Putting the icon last conflicts with 103b. KOM Kitty takeover (from Jan 5) turns the home-screen icon orange, and that needs the icon and manifest pipeline. Either build the fred icon before 103b, or drop the Kitty icon from 103b as the handoff already allows.
(4) Hanukkah (Dec 4) and Thanksgiving (Nov 26) are closer than Kitty. If holiday looks should show this season, 103a must land within about 3 weeks. Otherwise state that the first holidays shown will be later ones.
(5) "Medium" is generous. Nothing here breaks or cannot work as written. Low to medium planning advice fits better.

Mostly right. Two adjustments:

1. "KOM Kitty only if it can land by Jan 2, otherwise next year" is too strict. The takeover phase runs Jan 5 to Mar 6 (HANDOFF.md line 24), so Kitty can still ship partway into the season. Only the 3-day chase would be missed. Better wording: aim for Jan 2; if it misses, ship the takeover phase when ready; and drop the orange home-screen icon for this season unless a cheap, revertible PWA icon swap is proven.

2. "Least reversible" for the icon is an unverified claim. Reverting the files is trivial, but installed home-screen icons update unevenly. I did not check whether the manifest and apple-touch-icon in index.html would update for existing installs. Whatever that check shows, putting the icon last as its own item stands.

Also, 99 needs 104's crew switch, so either fold "Show the crew" into 99 (as the finding implies) or build 104 before 99.

title: Race-win scene (102) would overlap the existing PR!! graffiti moment and its play-once rules
rec: Make the race site part of the graffiti moment (one celebration), reuse GF_KEY's once and imported rules, and render the share PNG by drawing the serialized SVG onto a canvas (works offline) rather than html2canvas. HANDOFF A says Coach Ashley appears at race wins and in onboarding, but no item 97-104 includes her: add her to 102 or drop that line.
ev: index.html:15254-15258: the Races graffiti card circles the time and pops 'PR!!' once per new race, per device (bluebird.graffitiSeen.v1); imported races never animate. Share today goes through html2canvas from cdnjs (index.html:7769, 13251), which shows 'Image tool did not load' offline and handles inline SVG poorly.
corr: The finding holds, with one change in emphasis. The html2canvas risk is about what 102 might reuse, not about something it states: 102 names no renderer. The recommendation should therefore be to name the renderer in 102 (serialized SVG drawn onto a canvas, which works offline) rather than to "replace html2canvas". The overlap with the graffiti only happens when the race is a PB. A place-only win (1st to 3rd without a PR) has no graffiti pop, so it would be 102's only celebration, and 102 still needs its own once-per-device and imported-race rules for that case. The simplest fix is for 102 to reuse GF_KEY and gfFresh.

Mostly right, with three adjustments. First, item 102 does not say to use html2canvas. The offline risk only applies if the builder reuses the existing share path, so this is a recommendation, not a defect in the plan. The claim that html2canvas handles inline SVG poorly is unverified because I did not test it. Second, the overlap needs the graffiti card's own condition: it circles the time only for an overall PR. A place 1–3 without a PR would show the race site with no graffiti, so the two collide only on PR races. Third, 'overlap' is about how the two are timed and specified. No layout clash was measured, because handoff/real has no Races screenshot with a race in it. Severity medium is fair because the plan step is underspecified as written.

The offline part is overstated. sw.js caches cdnjs scripts cache-first (isLib), and index.html loads html2canvas as a normal script tag on every page load. After one online visit, sharing works offline. The toast appears only on a first-ever offline launch, or on an offline launch right after a cache version bump (activate deletes the old caches). The claim that html2canvas handles inline SVG poorly was not checked against FW's SVG. Drawing the serialized SVG onto a canvas is still the simpler and more reliable route, but the reason is that it needs no library, not that sharing is broken offline today. The recommendation stands: make the race site part of the graffiti moment, reuse GF_KEY's play-once and imported-race rules, and either add Coach Ashley to 102 (plus an onboarding item) or drop that line from section A. Severity medium is fair.

title: wxSky prints sample weather unless the app passes read:false
rec: Acceptance for 98 and 99: always call wxSky with {read:false} and render the app's own reading HTML, plus a test that no WX sample string appears in the DOM.
ev: weather.js:53 falls back to WX[k].t and .s when opt.t or opt.s is missing, e.g. clouds '55° → 60°', 'Cloudy · warming to 60° by 1:30'. Passing only t gives real temperature plus a made-up sub line.
corr: The finding is right, but the recommendation goes slightly too far for item 99. Using {t, s} there is fine as long as both come from the app's own forecast. The acceptance for 98 and 99 should be: either call wxSky with {read:false} and render the app's own reading, or always pass both t and s from the app's forecast, never just one. Add a test that no WX[k].t or WX[k].s sample string appears in the DOM. For item 98 specifically, {read:false} plus the app's existing reading matches "Keep the app's own reading" in HANDOFF.md.

The finding is only partly right for item 98. As written (HANDOFF.md:99), item 98 does not call wxSky at all. It places `FW.bird({wear: FW.WX[kind].wear})` into the app's own living sky and keeps "the app's own reading and gauge tiles untouched". So the risk only applies if the builder uses wxSky or wxCard there; wxCard also prints the mock WX[k].tiles. The risk is real for item 99 (HANDOFF.md:104), where the sky card shows a reading. There, requiring {read:false} on every call is too strict: passing both t and s is a supported, documented use. Better acceptance for 98 and 99: never call wxCard. Either call wxSky with {read:false} and render the app's own escaped reading, or always pass both t and s and never an empty one. Add a test that no WX[*].t, .s or tile string appears in the DOM for any of the nine skies.

This is the bundle's documented default, not a hidden bug: HANDOFF.md:77 already describes read:false and {t,s}. The real risk is passing partial options (only t, or only s): the gap gets silently filled with sample text. Fix: in 98 and 99, always pass read:false and render the app's own reading, or always pass both t and s. Add a test that no WX[k].t or WX[k].s string appears in the DOM. The same applies to the unexported wxCard (weather.js:56-58), which always prints the sample WX[k].tiles, so it should never be ported.

title: Full names and body notes for 19 real people ship to every client, even with names off
rec: Ship first names only (or no names) and drop team and quirk from the runtime bundle; keep them in the design files. With names off, a strip of faces means nothing to most riders, so give the crew a job (cheering on race wins, a tip on tap) rather than decoration on the pre-Crunch page.
ev: FW.FRIENDS entries include name, team and quirk, e.g. {name:'Ryan Warren', team:'Fitness Lab', quirk:'Legendary calves…'} (cast.js:234-252), in a public JS file. 'Show their names' only hides the label on screen.
corr: This is an improvement at low severity, not medium. All 19 consented, so it is not a privacy breach. The improvement still holds: the runtime code never reads team or quirk. Strip team and quirk (with the home towns) from the runtime FRIENDS array and keep them in the design files. Ship only what is shown: first names, or a short display name used only when 'Show their names' is on. This makes the bundle a little smaller and puts nothing beyond the drawn figures into public JS, which is all the consent clearly covers. Giving the crew a job (cheering on race wins, a tip on tap) is a separate product suggestion. It does not follow from this evidence.

What holds, at low severity: `team` and `quirk` are never read at runtime. The only FRIENDS uses are FRIENDS[i].o in cast.js:259, weather.js:40 and world.js:49. No code reads .name, .team or .quirk inside the bundle (the app would read .name for the names switch). Yet both fields ship in a public JS file, and they include design notes and hometowns of real people: 'Westfield, IN', 'Carmel, IN', 'Denver, CO', 'Runner · Carmel, IN', 'Great Dane dad', 'Legendary calves', and 'Frustrated… staring at a flat tyre'. The consent covers showing these people in the app. Whether it also covers publishing hometowns and descriptive notes is not stated (unverified). Recommendation: strip team and quirk from the runtime FRIENDS (keep them in the design sources or a build-time-only table), and keep name, because the item-104 names switch needs it. Treat this as low-severity privacy hygiene, worth a quick check with Mark on whether the consent covers hometowns.

Low-severity polish, not medium. The crew gave consent (HANDOFF.md:21) and names must ship because of the "Show their names" switch in item 104. Still, `team` and `quirk` in FW.FRIENDS (cast.js:234-252) are never used at runtime, so they are design notes published in a public JS file. Strip them from the shipped bundle (for example in build-bundle.py) and keep them in the design sources. Keep `name` for the names switch. First names only could be offered as an option, but nothing requires it.
notes: REAL: The facts are right, but the severity and the privacy framing are too strong. I checked the source and the shipped bundle. cast.js:234-254 defines FRIENDS with 19 entries. Each one has a full name, a team or town, and a quirk. The towns include "Westfield, IN", "Carmel, IN" and "Denver, CO", and one quirk reads "Great Dane dad". All 19 quirk strings are inside /Users/markmccabe/Downloads/handoff/fred-world.js; `grep -o quirk` finds 19. title: Night sky in item 98 reverses item 87's decision without saying so
rec: State the change in item 98 ('replaces 87.1(i)') and update item 87's QA, so a later reviewer doesn't flag it as a regression.
ev: QUEUE.md item 87 1(i): a clear night shows no sky and keeps the static moon icon; QA 'A night ride shows no sky.' Item 98 maps a clear night to FW 'night' and adds it to ?sky=.
corr: The finding is correct as stated. One addition: item 98 should also say what happens to item 87's static moon icon on a clear night, whether it stays, moves into the night sky, or is replaced. It should also add `night` to 87's ?sky= list and Done line, not only to its QA line.

The finding is right. One addition makes it sharper. Item 98 as written cannot work literally, because wxSkyOf(w) returns null for a clear night (origin/main index.html:10642, 10649-10654). There is nothing to map to 'night' unless item 98 also changes wxSkyPick: add 'night' to its order when wxDark(w) is true, or map null+wxDark to 'night'. Item 98 should say it replaces 87.1(i). It should also say the null branch in wxSkyPick and its comment are changed, and the static moon icon is dropped or kept. Item 87's QA line "A night ride shows no sky" (QUEUE.md:1448) should be updated to match.
notes: REAL: I checked the text and it holds. QUEUE.md item 87 (line 1371) says in 1(i): "clear at night (is_day 0 for the whole window) → no sky; keep today's static moon icon". Its QA list says "A night ride shows no sky.", and its Done note says "a clear night keeps the moon". The ?sky= QA list there names eight skies and has no night. HANDOFF.md item 98 (lines 98-101) says "a clear night → `night`", adds night stars that twinkle, and says "all nine skies (`?sky=` QA param, add `night`)". So item 98 reverses an earlier decision without saying so, and a builder or reviewer who follows 87's QA would call the night sky a regression. Low severity is right: this is only a spec-wording gap, not broken behaviour. I did not render the night sky.

title: Nested settings objects work against item 96's per-field merge
rec: Use flat keys (crewShow, crewNames, holidayThemes, worldMotion); keep rider as one unit, which is fine. Build 100, 103 and 104 only after q96 is merged.
ev: Item 96 stamps each top-level settings key. Section E adds settings.crew={show,names} and settings.rider (13 subkeys) as single units, so a names change on one device and a show change on another would conflict.
corr: Nothing here breaks a rule. Item 96 itself (QUEUE.md:1822) allows a nested section to be one unit, "such as volume, caf, bikes", and existing settings already sync that way. So settings.crew as one object is allowed by the spec; it is just a weaker choice. Splitting it into crewShow and crewNames is cheap and removes the two-switch conflict. The rider object has the same problem (for example, a helmet changed on one device and the kit on another), and keeping it as one unit, as recommended, is an accepted tradeoff, not a fix. The real impact is small: both changes have to be made on two devices before either syncs.

Partly overstated. holidayThemes and worldMotion are already flat top-level keys in section E (HANDOFF.md:133-134), so only settings.crew needs splitting, into crewShow and crewNames. Keeping rider as one unit matches item 96, which allows nested sections as one unit. This is an optional improvement, not a spec conflict. Building items 100, 103 and 104 after q96 is merged is sensible because they add synced settings keys, but I did not check what item 103 contains.

The finding is partly right. Keeping crew as one unit matches item 96's rule (QUEUE.md:1822 lets a nested section be one unit), so this is an optional polish, not a conflict with q96. The only practical gain from flat keys is splitting crew into crewShow and crewNames. holidayThemes and worldMotion are already flat in section E (HANDOFF.md:133-134), so they need no change. Keeping rider as one unit is fine. Building 100, 103 and 104 after q96 is merged is sensible sequencing, so the new keys get field stamps from the start. It is not required, though: under the pre-q96 whole-doc sync they would just sync like every other setting does today.

HANDOFF.md section E (lines 131-134) adds settings.crew = { show, names } as one nested object. The newer stamp takes the whole object, and the older device's change is undone. That is exactly the cross-device loss item 96 was written to prevent. holidayThemes and worldMotion are already flat keys in section E, so only crew needs changing.
